NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                           Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Environmental Safeguard Specialist (ESS)  

No: MW-NLGFC-563908-CS-INDIV

Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

 

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Environmental Safeguard Specialist (ESS) on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Environmental Safeguard Specialist (ESS) tenable at the NLGFC Offices.

 

The terms of Reference (TORs) for Environmental Safeguard Specialist (ESS) are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The Environnmental Safeguard Specilaist will ensure that GESD 2.0 activities comply with the Worlad Bank ESF and ESH guidelines as outlined in the governing Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), and Project Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) including all the supporting management plans as appropriate

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. coordination and provision of technical supervision, monitor and report on Environment safeguards in line with the national laws and in conformity with the Environmental and Social Framework of the World Bank and international best practices under the project;
  2. Provision of preventive and protective measures, including modification, substitution, or elimination of environmental risks and impacts; and
  3. Design and development of training programme for district officers, contractors and workers etc.
  4. Support the eligible local authorities in conducting environmental and social screening followed by the timely development and disclosure of Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) of all sub-project activities implemented by local authorities with the aim of incorporating due processes as standard practice in social and environmental safeguards implementation;
  5. Conduct reviews of ESMPs of all the subprojects developed by the local authorities in compliance with Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and the Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), RAPs, and other relevant E and S instruments to ensure quality and timely submission;
  6. Provide and review environmental and social inputs into the planning, design and contracting of investments, including the preparation of tender documents in line with the Environmental and Social Frameworks (ESF);
  7. Develop and implement an internal administrative tracking system for the PIU in order to monitor the progress of project activities in terms of meeting environmental and social safeguard requirements. The system will include the planning, assessment, approval, implementation and monitoring phases of GESD 2.0 Project activities. The system will be computer based (using a spread sheet or Microsoft Access) and designed for easy data entry and report generation. Reports generated by the system should be simple to produce, showing progress of a specific project activity, and highlight critical items such as pending or overdue actions;
  8. Design and deliver, or arrange for the delivery of, an environmental and social safeguards capacity building program for local authorities’ staff and other relevant stakeholders with the purpose of strengthening capacity of local authorities to implement environmental and social safeguard requirements effectively within the context of larger GESD 2.0 activities;
  9. Following up implementation of environmental screening and implementation of ESMPs and Social response operations at sector and district levels through EDOs (local authority staff);
  10. Undertaking review of CESMPs and provide feedback to local authorities;
  11. Undertake spots checks on compliance monitoring of Contractors Environmental and Social Management Plan for PBG sub-projects;
  12. Undertaking site visits and reviewing contractors' compliance with site-specific CESMPs, Labour Management Procedures (LMPs), Codes of Conducts etc. including determining and suggesting remedial actions in collaboration with the Environmental Expert and Occupational Safety and Health (OHS) Expert;
  13. Preparation of non-compliance reports and keeping track of respective responses/actions undertaken and preparation of periodic Environmental Compliance Monitoring Reports;
  14. Participating at the official meetings with the Bank and other forums related to the project;
  15. Undertake internal E&S Audits and support consultants in the preparation of external E&S Audits, and track the implementation of the corrective and remedial action plans by the district and municipal councils;
  16. Provide inputs and materials to Communication Specialist for devising communication strategy, knowledge products and dissemination of results;
  17. Timely preparation and submission of monthly, quarterly, annual and period reports to the Project Coordinator, Executive Director and World Bank task team; and
  18. Performing any other duties as may be necessary for the effective implementation of the project as assigned by Project Coordinator and or Director of Social and Economic Services.

 

4.      Qualifications and Experience

 

The candidate should meet the following qualifications:

 

  1. Master’s Degree in Environmental Sciences, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources Management, Environmental Policy and Analysis; Environmental Management and Economics;
  2. A minimum of 8 years of experience in the field of environmental management at National level or international organization, and donor projects handling environmental and social aspects of planning, assessing and managing civil works projects of various scale in Malawi or similar African countries;
  3. Working knowledge of World Bank environmental and social frameworks, especially Environmental and Social Assessment (ESS1), Land Acquisition, Restriction on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement (ESS5), and have demonstrated experience in successfully preparing ESIAs, ESMPs and RAPs in line with World Bank standards, policies will be considered an advantage;
  4. Working knowledge of regulations in Malawi related to Environmental and Social issues;
  5. Experience with designing and delivering capacity building programs;
  6. Familiarity with Article VI of Paris 21 Agreement; environmental, social and economic conditions prevailing in Malawi or similar African countries;
  7. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, as well as team participation and management skills;
  8. Strong organizational and communications skills and ability to interface with grassroots, district and sector players in the discipline;
  9. Demonstrated Computer Skill (Proficiency in using computer desktop application MS Office (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint);
  10. Knowledge of the decentralized local government systems in Malawi; and
  11. Upholding of anticorruption and antibribery ethics

 

5. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

 

The Contract is for a period of 3 years with yearly review. The renewal of the contract is upon satisfactory appraisal results.

6. LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

The Environmental Safeguards Specialist will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Environmental Safeguards Specialist will occasionally be required to travel to all local government authorities in Malawi where the GESD 2.0 Project is implementing its activities to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation (environmental safeguards).

7.REPORTING

The Environmental Safeguards Specialist will report to the Project Coordinator for all administrative operations and to the Head of Environmental Safeguards Unit and Director of Social and Economic Services at NLGFC for technical issues, and will work in collaboration with local authorities and other specialists under the project, Social Safeguards Specialist, Occupational Health and Safety Specialist, and Project Engineers.

 

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and  A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations

Interested applicants who meet the above requirements should submit application letters together with concise Curriculum Vitae (CV), National ID, and copies of relevant certificates to the address below not later than 17.30 hours on Friday, 11th September 2026.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES

 

Country:                       Angola

Project´s Name:           Projecto de Transformação da Agropecuária Familiar (MOSAP 3)

Loan No.:                     BIRD-9396 – AO

Assignment Title:        Selection of an Individual Consultant to conduct a procurement audit covering   the 2023, 2024, and 2025 fiscal years.

Reference No.:                        179/C3/C/MOSAP3/26

The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (MINAGRIF) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Smallholder Agricultural Transformation Project (MOSAP 3) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) includes (i) reviewing the procurement, contracting, and implementation processes and evaluate the quality, timeliness, reliability and appropriateness of comments and no-objections issued by the Bank for a sample of contracts, to confirm their consistency with the Legal Agreements and associated documents and ensuring that procurement, contracting and disbursement is being carried out in accordance with WB Guidelines and procedures; (ii) verifying technical compliance, physical completion and price competitiveness of each contract in the selected representative sample of contracts and expressing a professional opinion on compliance by the procurement processes with the general principle of economy and efficiency, equal opportunities, transparency; (iii) reviewing the responsibility matrix for the procurement function in the organization, delegation of procurement authority and internal control functions; the capacity of implementing agencies in handling procurement efficiently, comment on the quality of procurement and contracting, and identify reasons for delays, if any and overall, how procurement management facilitates project implementation; (iv) analyzing the risks in the various steps of procurement cycle (definition and quantification of requirements, approval of requisition, supplier sourcing, selection of procurement method, selection of contract type, bid opening and evaluation proceedings, formation of evaluation committees, approval of award, contract management, records management, use of financial securities, management of warranty/maintenance obligations, disposal of assets) and identifying any indicators of questionable standards of ethics in the procurement management and oversight environment that make the processes vulnerable to fraud and corruption or collusive and obstructive practices, and report any suspicious cases; (v) providing advice to MOSAP 3 on procurement and internal control issues and coordination with other ministries and departments on matters arising from each audit and record them in Action Plans (IPR Reports) recommending operations needed to improve project procurement performance consistent with program objectives, accuracy and completeness of the procurement records in the filling system, timely preparation of procurement information, policies and procedures that must be adopted by project management and procurement staff in ensuring orderly, economic, effective and efficient procurement operations in light of deficiencies; and all others required in the Terms of References.

The estimated level of effort is one person-month, and the contract will have a duration of 4 months, wherein it is expected that the individual consultant carries out site visit missions of about thirty (30) Calendar days. The consultant is expected to commence services no later than January 15th, 2027.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Smallholder Agriculture Transformation Project (MOSAP 3) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The short listing criteria are: [a] Be proficient in procurement and contract management, [b] Have a degree in Agronomy, Business administration, Project Management, Law, Engineering; [c] Have completed at least 3 similar contracts for the past 5 years; [d] Have at least 10 years of relevant experience with World Bank’s Procurement procedures and having worked as a Senior Procurement Specialist in World Bank funded Operations for at least eight (8) years; and [e] Fluency in English and working knowledge of Portuguese language.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” [Ed. November2020 (“Procurement Regulations”)], setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. The document in reference may be obtained through the following: link:https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/1783315330658711950290022020/original/ProcurementRegulations.pdf.

An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants (ICS) set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, from 08:00 AM to 03:30 PM.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) by September 15th, 2026 at 15:00 (Angola time).

NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                         Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                                  Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Financial Management Specialist (FMS) 

No: MW-NLGFC-563892-CS-INDIV

                                     Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026        

 

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Financial Management Specialist (FMS) on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Financial Management Specialist (FMS) tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for Financial Management Specialist (FMS) are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The objective of the Financial Management Specialist position is to ensure the sound financial management of the project in compliance with the Financing Agreement, Government of Malawi public financial management regulations, including the Public Finance Management Act and related regulations, treasury instructions and IFMIS desk instructions, project operations manual, and World Bank financial management requirements. The Financial Management Specialist will be responsible for planning, budgeting, accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, funds management, audit coordination, and financial compliance to ensure that project resources are used efficiently, effectively, transparently, and for their intended purposes.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. Preparation of Financial Statements in accordance with the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) of the Project within six months from the end of the financial year; 
  2. Coordination of the preparation of a consolidated project budget, cash flow forecasts, execution and monitoring including liaising with key ministries and departments for budget planning and execution; 
  3. Ensure that the Project resources are used in accordance with the conditions of the relevant financing agreement, Project Operation Manual with due attention to economy and efficiency, and only for the purposes for which the financing was provided;
  4. Preparation of disbursement requests and financial justifications for the project and submit to Treasury and the World Bank;
  5. Produce monthly, quarterly, semi-annual and annual financial reports from central and district levels, as part of the implementation of the Project;
  6. Coordinate closely with procurement and technical teams against the work plan and project objectives to ensure comprehensive mitigation measures are taken.
  7. Ensure that all necessary supporting documents, records, and accounts with physical documents have been maintained in respect of all project activities, including expenditures reported using Statement of Expenditures (SOE) or Interim Financial Reports (IFRs) methods of reporting.
  8. Periodically review the performance of control functions to ensure that internal controls are sufficient and functioning correctly and that Financial Performance of the Project is Satisfactory;
  9. Coordinate project external and internal audits and responding to management letter;
  10. Coordinate as necessary with Internal and External Audit, Government of Malawi and Bank supervision missions, including attending to follow up on findings and recommendations;
  11. Maintain accurate and traceable schedules for VAT and timely remittance of tax deductions to the Malawi Revenue Authority;
  12. Advise the Project Coordinator and Director of Finance on all financial and control considerations of the project;
  13. Supervise and strengthen the capacity of PIT and local authorities in the knowledge of the rules and procedures of the financial management of the World Bank;
  14. Upholding of anticorruption and antibribery ethics; and
  15. Undertake all other duties and responsibilities commensurate with the role and level of this position as may be requested by the Project Coordinator.

4.      Qualifications and Experience

 

The candidate should meet the following qualifications:

       i.  A Bachelor’s degree in accounting and finance/ or equivalent qualification;

  1. A professional accounting qualification such as CPA (MW), ACCA, CIMA etc.;
  2. A master’s degree in accounting; auditing; finance; business administration will be an added advantage;
  3. A minimum of 8 years of experience in financial management in the public sector;
  4. Experience of financial management in donor funded projects and/or audit experience is considered an advantage; 
  5. Member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in Malawi (ICAM);  
  6. Outstanding numeracy, planning, organizing and controlling skills;
  7. Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills, communication and analytical skills;
  8. Ability to work in teams and articulation with a diverse audience;
  9. Good computer skills and proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and PowerPoint, etc.);
  10. Ability and experience in training / mentoring staff in the area of financial management is an advantage;
  11. Willingness to work under pressure, tight timelines, and with minimum supervision;
  12. Knowledge of audit techniques; and
  13. Upholding of anticorruption and ant bribery ethics.

5. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

 

6. LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

 

The Financial Management Specialist (FMS) will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Financial Management Specialist will occasionally be required to travel to district authorities in Malawi to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation (financial management).

7.REPORTING

The Financial Management Specialist will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Director of Finance and Fiscal Decentralization at NLGFC for all technical matters, and will support the local authorities’ financial management teams.

.

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and a Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant(INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information including the detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 7:30 hours to 12:00 hours and from 13:00 hours to 16:30 hours except on Weekends and Public Holidays

 

9. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Interested applicants who meet the above requirements should submit application letters together with concise Curriculum Vitae (CV), National ID, and copies of relevant certificates to the address below not later than 17.30 hours on Friday 11th  September  2026.

 

The National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) is committed to diversifying Gender equality in its operations and strongly encourages women to apply for the above vacant position.

 

The Executive Director

National Local Government Finance Committee

Area 14, Red Cross Building

Presidential Way

P.O. Box 31162

Lilongwe 3

Or through the following email address:

recruitment@nlgfc.gov.mw /ed@nlgfc.gov.mw

Only shortlisted applicants will be considered for further assessments

NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                      

                            Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                                  Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Project Coordinator

No: MW-NLGFC-563879-CS-INDIV

                     

                                          Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

 

  1. Introduction Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Project Coordinator on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Project Coordinator at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for Project Coordinator are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The objective of the Project Coordinator position is to provide strategic leadership and day-to-day management of the project to ensure the timely and effective delivery of project activities and achievement of project objectives. The Project Coordinator will coordinate planning, budgeting, procurement, contract administration, financial management, environmental and social safeguards, human resource management, governance arrangements, stakeholder engagement, and implementation support missions, while ensuring compliance with Government and donor requirements.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. Coordination: Ensure cross-component and cross-institutional coordination and linkages through information sharing, joint implementation of project activities and provide strategic guidance and coordination to the PIT members on all project related activities in order to keep workflow on track;

 

  1. Planning: Spearhead and coordinate the preparation and implementation of Project’s Annual Procurement Plan in line with agreed timelines and budgets; spearhead the planning and implementation of project activities to each activity specific goals and project goals overall in coordination with the PIT technical specialists and relevant key stakeholders; ensure that detailed activity plans are prepared and monitored; be proactive and provide solutions to bring forward delayed/off-track activities; ensure alignment of all activities with the annual work plan and budget;  

 

  1. Budgeting: Lead the timely development of consolidated project budgets for planned activities, cash flow forecasts, executing and monitoring of budgets, and ensure that the activity budgets are aligned with the annual work plan and consistent; coordinate with the PIT Financial Management Specialist and liaise with key ministries and departments and local authorities for budget planning and execution;

 

  1. Procurement: In coordination with the PIT Procurement Specialist ensure the timely preparation, execution and updated of procurement plans at the central level and at the district level; liaise with all relevant stakeholders; ensure that all procurements for consultants, goods and works under each procurement plan are carried out in accordance with the agreed procedures, including the Financing Agreement; the World Bank Procurement Guidelines/regulations and the Government of Malawi Public Procurement and Disposal of Assets Act 2025 and World Bank policies.

 

  1. Contract Management: Lead the management of contracts for consultants and other service providers, and work with all PIT members to evaluate potential problems and technical hitches and timely develop solutions;

 

  1. Financial Management: Manage financial resources of the project in coordination with the PIT Financial Management Specialist; ensure that all project activities are executed in accordance with the Financing Agreements, and the policies and standards of all relevant implementing agencies; ensure strict adherence to project budgets by monitoring expenses and implementing cost-saving measures; and ensure the timely preparation of financial statements and audits according to the Financing Agreement; ensure that the project is timely audited by the National Audit Office and submit an annual audit report to Government of Malawi and World Bank  not later than 30th September.

 

  1. Environmental and Social Safeguards: Ensure that all environment and social safeguards are adhered in all activities financed by the GESD 2.0 project and are managed in accordance with World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), and Good International Industry Practice (GIIP); coordinate with relevant PIT specialists, district officials and relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies to ensure eligible local authorities develop and implements environmental safeguards issues in all the sub project sites;

 

  1. Project Office Management and Staff Management: Manage the PIT on a day-to-day basis; coordinate and supervise administrative activities necessary for the successful implementation of GESD 2.0; supervise and be responsible for the specialists’ time commitment and performance on the project; ensure timely preparation and submission of all consultants reports from the Project Engineers; Financial Management Specialist; Procurement Specialist; Monitoring and Evaluation Officer; Safeguards Specialist; Occupation and Health Specialist; Environmental Safeguard Specialist and all implementing agencies; undertake staff performance appraisals with support from  NLGFC; and

 

  1. Oversight Meetings, Monitoring and Evaluation, and Supervision: Facilitate key project meetings (quarterly project progress meetings, meetings of the Project Steering Committee, meetings of the Project Technical Committee) and liaison with stakeholders regularly and submit minutes of respective meetings within 48 hours; serve as Secretary to the PTC and supervise and ensure execution of any decisions approved by the PTC; ensure that all activities at central and at district level are carried out according to the provisions of the Malawi Government legislation and as stipulated in the Project Operations Manual and Financing Agreement; prepare and submit monthly, quarterly and annual project progress reports to the Executive Director and the World Bank task team; prepare and submit bi-annual updates on project progress against the project results framework; organize World Bank implementation support missions, including follow up on mission recommendations.

4.      Qualifications and Experience

 

The candidate should meet the following qualifications:

 

  1. A Master's Degree in Project Management, Economics, Development Studies, Finance/Accounting, Business Administration, or Engineering from a recognized institution;
  2. At least 8 years relevant working experience in senior positions or project management positions in public sector projects with a focus on planning, budget management and execution;
  3. At least 5 years of relevant working experience with Malawi’s Public Financial Management Structures; experience in fiscal decentralization is considered an asset;
  4. Demonstrated proficiency with project and budget management software / tracking tools, project fiduciary procedures;
  5. Demonstrated problem-solving skills and managerial skills, including proactivity;
  6. Demonstrated experience to work effectively with and in multi-sectoral teams;
  7. Good computer skills and proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and PowerPoint, etc.);
  8. Highly motivated with excellent planning, analytical, communications and interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy;
  9. Experience in working with the World Bank, multi-lateral development partners or bilateral partners is considered an asset;
  10. Willingness to work under pressure, tight timelines, and with minimum supervision;
  11. Excellent communication and report writing skills and be fluent in English; and
  12. Upholding of anticorruption and antibribery ethics.

 

5. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

 

6. LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

The Project Coordinator will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Project Coordinator will occasionally be required to travel to district authorities in Malawi to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation.

7.REPORTING

The Project Coordinator will report to the Executive Director of National Local Government Finance Committee for all the project progress and implementation issues.

.

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information including the detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 7:30 hours to 12:00 hours and from 13:00 hours to 16:30 hours except on Weekends and Public Holidays

 

9. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Interested applicants who meet the above requirements should submit application letters together with concise Curriculum Vitae (CV), National ID, and copies of relevant certificates to the address below not later than 17.30 hours on Friday, 11th September, 2026.

procnotices.notice_text:
REPÚBLICA DE MOÇAMBIQUE

MINISTÉRIO DAS OBRAS PÚBLICAS, HABITAÇÃO E RECURSOS HDRICOS

DIRECÇÃO NACIONAL DE ABASTECIMENTO DE ÁGUA E SANEAMENTO

 

PROJECTO DE ÁGUA SEGURA PARA VILAS E ZONAS RURAIS -P173518

SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE

 

CONTRATAÇÃO DE SERVIÇOS DE CONSULTORIA PARA APOIAR NA MELHORIA DE RECURSOS VISUAIS DO DASHBOARD DO PROJECTO ÁGUA SEGURA

 

GRANT. N.º D941-MZ

Ref. N.º MZ-DNAAS-85-CS-INDV

 

1. O Governo de Moçambique, recebeu do Banco Mundial o financiamento de 150 Milhões de Dólares Americanos para o Projeto Água Segura para Zonas Rurais e Vilas. O principal resultado do Projecto é aumentar os serviços de água e saneamento geridos de forma segura em pequenas cidades e áreas rurais seleccionadas das províncias de Nampula e Zambézia, na Região Norte de Moçambique.

 

2. O escopo dos serviços para a consultoria inclui diagnóstico inicial, mas não se limita à: (i) Propor ajustes técnicos nas bases de dados e ferramenta em uso pelo Projecto para o Dashboard (Kobo, Excell e Power BI) e criação de novos componentes visuais caso se justifique o seu uso e definir as responsabilidades de cada um dos Usuários do Dashboard assim como a disponibilização de dados para o mesmo; ii) Implementar regras de validação; criar uma visão da qualidade dos dados (integridade, actualização, erros); fornecer um dicionário de dados e um mapa de transformação; configurar atualizações programadas com alertas de erro e atribuir a propriedade dos dados para controle de qualidade; iii) Configurar acesso baseado em funções para utilizadores DNAAS/AIAS/provinciais/distritais; fornecer uma matriz de acesso baseado em funções e uma lista de acesso; documentar as responsabilidades dos utilizadores (entrada de dados, controlo de qualidade, verificação).; iv) Aplicar um tema consistente alinhado com o estilo utilizado pelo Projecto/Governo/Banco Mundial; redesenhar layouts para melhorar a clareza; garantir acessibilidade (contraste, tamanho da fonte); permitir a tradução português/inglês e visualização por província/distrito quando aplicável; v) Optimizar consultas, DAX e recursos visuais; definir e implementar estratégias de atualização (por exemplo, atualização incremental); Documentar as melhorias de desempenho alcançadas em relação à linha de base.

 

3. Os Termos de Referência (TdRs) detalhados para a consultoria podem ser solicitados através do seguinte endereço: procurementpas@gmail.com

 

4. A Direcção Nacional de Abastecimento de Água e Saneamento (DNAAS), convida os consultores individuais qualificados, a manifestar seu interesse em prestar os serviços. Os consultores interessados deverão apresentar informação demonstrando possuir qualificações necessárias e experiência relevante para a execução dos serviços (CV, descrição de serviços similares, experiência em condições semelhantes, disponibilidade, etc.).

5. O consultor deve possuir, pelo menos, as seguintes qualificações e experiência: (i) Apresentar o portfólio de trabalhos anteriores em visualização de dados; ii) Ao menos 5 anos de experiência em visualização de dados, BI e desenho web; iii) Experiência comprovada em Power BI (modelagem de dados, DAX, controle de acesso, ajuste de desempenho); a apresentação de certificações será considerada uma vantagem;  iv) Experiência na integração do KoboToolbox e do Excel (ou ferramentas similares) em fluxos de trabalho de BI; v)  Experiência e familiaridade com a monitoria e avaliação aplicada ao sector de WASH será considerada uma vantagem vi)  Conhecimento e habilidade sobre as boas práticas de design digital; e v)  Experiência com gestão e governança da qualidade de dados, workshops com partes interessadas e formação (necessária a proficiência em português).

 

6. A atenção dos Consultores interessados é chamada para a Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 dos "Regulamentos de Aquisição para Mutuários do IPF" do Banco Mundial, de fevereiro de 2025 ("Regulamentos de Contratação Pública"), que estabelecem a política do Banco Mundial sobre conflito de interesses.

 

7. O Consultor será seleccionado de acordo com o método de Selecção de Consultor Individual conforme estabelecido no Regulamento de Aquisições.

8. Mais informações podem ser obtidas no endereço abaixo, no horário normal de expediente (7h30 às 15h30). As manifestações de interesse devem ser entregues por escrito a:

Endereço: Ministério das Obras Públicas, Habitação e Recursos Hídricos

Av. Karl Marx nº 606, P.O. Box 268 * Maputo, Telefone: 326081, R/C

Departamento de Aquisições,

Email: procurementpas@gmail.com

 

As Manifestações de Interesse deverão ser entregues em versão física na língua portuguesa, no endereço acima e por e-mail para os endereços acima indicados até 15:30 horas do dia 04 de Setembro de 2026.

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

 

 

Republic of Botswana

Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Project (HEPRR)

Health, Nutrition and Population

Loan No. 98750 |

Grant: Livable Planet Fund (LPF)

Project ID No. P510190

 

The Government of the Republic of Botswana, through the Ministry of Health and the Botswana Medicines Regulatory Authority (BoMRA), has received financing in the amount of US40,000,000 from the World Bank (IBRD Loan No. 98750) and a grant of US3,000,000 from the IBRD Surplus-Funded Livable Planet Fund (LPF), toward the cost of the Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Project (HEPRR), and intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this project. This project is part of the regional HEPRR Program implemented under the World Bank's Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA), spanning 11 countries across Eastern and Southern Africa.

The project will include the following components:

Component 1: Strengthening the Preparedness and Resilience of the Botswana Health System (US$34.4 million). This component, implemented primarily by BoMRA, will support the construction of a National Drug Quality Control Laboratory (NDQCL) incorporating climate-resilient measures, and the refurbishment of BoMRA Regional Offices. It will also finance the procurement of laboratory equipment and supplies for the NDQCL, the supply and delivery of Vital, Essential, and Necessary (VEN) commodities for warehouse stockpiling, and software development for a National Product Catalogue (National eLMIS system).

Component 2: Improving the Detection of and Response to Health Emergencies through a Multisectoral Approach (US$5 million). This component will support renovations to the National Public Health Laboratory (NPHL) to address audit findings and support accreditation transition. It will also finance the procurement of laboratory equipment and supplies for the NPHL and the procurement and maintenance of emergency stockpiles. Consulting services under this component include technical advisory and institutional capacity support for surveillance, laboratory diagnostics, and emergency management; development and implementation of clinical case management guidelines for priority health events; and other advisory services in support of multisectoral emergency preparedness and response.

Component 3: Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation (US$3.6 million). This component will finance the supply and delivery of project vehicles, as well as consulting services for project management support, monitoring and evaluation, and fiduciary oversight. Procurement through open international competitive procedures under this component includes individual consultant assignments for the Mid-Term Review and the Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICRR).

Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) (US$0). This component provides the capacity to rapidly reallocate project funds in the event of an eligible crisis or emergency. Specific procurement activities will be determined if and when the CERC is activated.

Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2025 edition) (Procurement Regulations) and is open to all eligible firms and individuals as defined in the Procurement Regulations. After project negotiations, the World Bank shall arrange the publication on its external website of the agreed initial procurement plan, and all subsequent updates once it has provided a no objection. All procurement activities are tracked through the World Bank's Systematic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement (STEP) system.

Specific procurement notices for contracts subject to open international competitive procurement will be announced, as they become available, on the World Bank's external  and in local newspapers of national circulation in Botswana.

Interested eligible firms and individuals who would wish to be considered for the provision of goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services for the above-mentioned project, or those requiring additional information, should contact the Borrower at the addresses below:

procnotices.notice_text:
NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                      Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                                  Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Project Engineer (2)

No: MW-NLGFC-563895-CS-INDIV/ MW-NLGFC-563897-CS-INDIV

                     

                                          Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring two Project Engineer on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of two (2) Project Engineer tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for two (2) Project Engineer) are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The Project Engineer (Specialist) shall lead, coordinate and support local authorities and all relevant ministries, departments and agencies in the design and implementation of the project. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will lead and have approving authority for preparing and/or interpreting designs, bill of quantities (BoQs), tendering and engineering cost estimates prepared. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will work closely with relevant district authorities, including district engineers, other officers and specialists in the PIT, including safeguards, Project Coordinator, NLGFC, MoLGRD and other relevant stakeholders, including but not limited to supervision consultants. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will support monitoring of the sub-projects and will address and manage technical engineering questions in local investment projects implemented by the local authorities that are financed by GESD 2.0. 

 

  1. Duties and Responsibilities of the Project Engineer (Consultant)

 

The Project Engineers (Consultants) will be responsible for providing technical leadership and engineering oversight to ensure that project activities are planned, designed, implemented, monitored, and completed in accordance with approved specifications, quality standards, budget, schedule, and applicable regulations.

 

Specific tasks will include the following:

 

  1. Coordinate and support all engineering functions and activities related to infrastructure construction and rehabilitation in the local authorities, namely Department of Planning and Development and Department of Public Works;
  2. Support data collection for all proposed sub-project sites to aid development and customisation of architectural designs, production of BoQs and engineering estimates, tendering processes and ensuring that designs are in conformity with results of site-specific resilience and risk related investigations and analysis;
  3. Ensure timely and correct submission of information into the Public Management Information System (PMIS) by local authorities;
  4. Provide technical support to the Local Authorities in project selection, reviewing annual investment plans, works designs, BoQs, costs estimate, tendering, supervision and monitoring;
  5. Coordinate topographic surveys for the design of infrastructure to be developed under the Project;
  6. Support local authorities in conducting initial site investigation;
  7. Facilitate the production of location maps and sketches if necessary for all engineering sites that need maintenance and repair (selected as subprojects under GESD 2.0);
  8. Support and if necessary lead the review and approval of submissions by design engineers, including ensuring timely submission of the same;
  9. Support and if necessary lead design options stakeholder consultations with communities and relevant departments so that their inputs are incorporated in the designs to ensure acceptance and ownership of solutions to be developed;
  10. Conduct technical supervision of all construction works ensuring that the works are implemented to the required standards, within the assigned cost and time;
  11. Check Supervision Consultant’s work so as to conduct verification of contractors’ payment claims for works done;
  12. Manage changes to engineering constructions works ensuring that any changes have no adverse effect on the project and they are undertaken following project works change protocols, including documentation;
  13. Facilitate preparation of work plans and budgets for local investment projects to ensure relevance to outputs and outcomes of local investment project;
  14. Support the preparation of schedule of works and materials for project activities in collaboration with relevant stakeholders;
  15. Review and assess contractors’ and consultants’ payment certificates for engineering works
  16. Prepare and conduct training programs for Local Authority technical staff involved in contract and procurement management; and other related activities as directed by the PIT;
  17. Ensure compliance with all statutory and regulatory requirements;
  18. Liaise with other project specialists and officers, including safeguards, occupational health & safety, procurement, and advise the PIT on all construction Engineering technical related matters;
  19. Collect projects’ progress reports from the LAs, liaise with the monitoring & evaluation officer in the PIT in producing reports for project activities, consolidate them and submit them to PIT/PC, Executive Director and World Bank Task Team;
  20. Preparation and timely submission of monthly, quarterly and annual engineering project progress reports and other reports to the Project Coordinator, Executive Director and the World Bank Task Team.
  21. Facilitating the review of Annual Investment Plans (AIPs) for Local authorities and provide guidance on cost and time estimates.

 

  1. Deliverables

 

Deliverables for the assignment correspond to the duties and responsibilities above. Specifically, they will comprise:

 

  1. Timely review of AIPs submitted by local authorities, including review of cost and time estimates;
  2. Reviewed and approved engineering designs and drawings.
  3. Technical specifications and BoQs.
  4. Engineering project progress reports and other reports timely compiled
  5. Site inspection reports.
  6. Quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) reports.
  7. Defects and corrective action reports.
  8. Monthly and quarterly progress reports, aligned with PMIS information.
  9. Physical progress monitoring reports.
  10. Work completion certificates.

 

  1. Performance Criteria

 

The following performance criteria will be used to assess the performance of the Project Engineer annually and based upon these assessments the contract with the project (GESD 2.0) may be continued or terminated:

  • 100% of required technical reports submitted on time.
  • At least 95% compliance with approved engineering specifications and quality standards.
  • Site inspections conducted according to approved supervision schedules.
  • 100% of contractor payment certificates reviewed and processed within agreed timelines.
  • All identified defects and non-compliance issues addressed within specified corrective action periods.
  • Minimal cost and schedule overruns attributable to technical deficiencies.
  • No major engineering failures or quality-related incidents.
  • Timely completion and handover of project infrastructure.
  • PMIS utilization by local authorities.

 

  1. Qualifications, Skills and Expertise

 

The candidate should meet the following minimum qualifications:

 

  1. Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering/Architecture/Quantity Surveying
  2. Master’s Degree in Construction/Engineering related field and ;
  3. Registration with an approved professional body, such as Malawi Engineering Institution/Board of Architects and Quantity Surveyors
  4. A minimum of 8 years of relevant working experience;
  5. Excellent communications, writing/reporting skills;
  6. Proficiency in computer aided design packages (AutoCAD, ArchCAD, GIS etc)
  7. Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Microsoft Project etc.);
  8. Strong organizational, self-starting and communications skills;
  9. Experience working with government institutions and organizations; working experience with local authorities in Malawi is considered an advantage;
  10. Highly motivated and enthusiastic person with excellent planning, analytical, communications and interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy; and
  11. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, as well as team participation and management skills

 

  1. Reporting Arrangements

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Director of Social and Economic Services at NLGFC for all technical matters, and will support local authorities’ in implementation of GESD 2.0 project.

 

  1. Location of Assignment

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Project Engineer (Consultant) will occasionally be required to travel to local government authorities in Malawi where the Project is implementing its activities to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation.

 

  1. Duration of Assignment

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

.

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information including the detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 7:30 hours to 12:00 hours and from 13:00 hours to 16:30 hours except on Weekends and Public Holidays

 

9. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Interested applicants who meet the above requirements should submit application letters together with concise Curriculum Vitae (CV), National ID, and copies of relevant certificates to the address below not later than 17.30 hours on Friday, 11th September 2026.

The National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) is committed to diversifying Gender equality in its operations and strongly encourages women to apply for the above vacant position.

recruitment@nlgfc.gov.mw/ ed@nlgfc.gov.mw

TÜRKYE FLOOD AND DROUGHT MANAGEMENT PROJECT (P179313)

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST FOR PROCUREMENT SPECIALIST

The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (MoAF) of Türkiye, Directorate General of Water Management (GDWM) has received financing from the World Bank (“the Bank”) toward the cost of the Türkiye Flood and Drought Management Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

DGWM serves as the co-implementing agency for the Project. The overall objective of the Project is to support climate change projections, determine their impacts on scenario-specific flood and drought disasters, and improve and expand existing early warning systems. It aims to strengthen the technical and operational capacities of all stakeholders for the uninterrupted and effective operation of the system.

DGWM has established a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) within its administrative structure to manage the project activities. DGWM intends to engage a Procurement Specialist (individual consultant) to provide technical support to the DGWM PIU in managing procurement activities under the Project. The Procurement Specialist will be responsible for planning and providing procurement services, including preparing procurement plans, bidding documents, evaluation reports, training activities and monitoring contract performance.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR), including the qualification requirements and scope of work for the assignment, can be found at the following web page address: https://www.tarimorman.gov.tr/SYGM/Sayfalar/Detay.aspx?SayfaId=187

Hiring Methodology

The Procurement Specialist will be selected through the ‘Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants’ method in accordance with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2023)”. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest.

Individuals currently working as procurement consultants on another World Bank-financed project may also compete, provided they meet the requirements for early termination of their existing contracts to avoid disruption in project implementation.

Duration and Place of Work

The Procurement Specialist is expected to commence work in September 2026 with a one-year contract having a two-month probation period. The Procurement Specialist will work on a full-time basis and will be located in Ankara, with potential travel to project sites as required.

Application Procedure

Interested eligible candidates should submit their CVs in both English and Turkish (in the format specified on the website), clearly indicating the position title and the reference number TR-DGWM-564534-CS-INDV in the subject line.

Applications must be delivered in PDF format via e-mail to the address below no later than September 9, 2026, at 16:00 (local time).

Contact Information:

Directorate General of Water Management (GDWM)

E-mail: sygm.worldbank@tarimorman.gov.tr

AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET SELECTION DE CONSULTANTS PAR LES EMPRUNTEURS DE LA BANQUE MONDIALE

N°002/MFBEPCI/SE/SG/SWEDD+/PM/2026

Recrutement d’un consultant individuel pour élaborer le manuel de procédure de  Laboratoire National de Contrôle Qualité des Médicaments (LNCQM).

 

N° de Don : IDA E2400 TD

Réf PPM : TD-SWEDD-TD -531397-CS-INDIV

 

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad a reçu un Don de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) N° E2400-TD, pour financer le coût du Projet pour l’Autonomisation des Femmes et le Dividende Démographique en Afrique Sub-Saharienne Plus (SWEDD+).

 

  1. Le Projet SWEDD+ a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce fonds, pour effectuer les paiements autorisés au titre de contrats suivants : Services de Consultant pour le recrutement d’un consultant individuel pour élaborer le manuel de procédure de  Laboratoire National de Contrôle Qualité des Médicaments (LNCQM).

 

  1. Les services de consultant (« Services ») consiste à élaborer le manuel de procédure de  Laboratoire National de Contrôle Qualité des Médicaments (LNCQM).

 

 

  1. Le Ministère des Finances, du Budget, de l’Économie, du Plan et de la Coopération Internationale (MFBEPCI) à travers le Projet SWEDD+ invite les cabinets (« Consultants ») admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits dans les termes de référence. Les consultant individuels intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et des expériences pertinentes pour l’exécution des Services. Les critères pour le choix du consultant sont les références techniques liées à des missions similaires, à savoir : Le consultant devra être titulaire d'un diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+4 minimum dans l'un des domaines suivants : management, administration des entreprises, gestion de projet, droit, finances, ou toute discipline connexe impliquant une formation à la structuration organisationnelle et à la rédaction formelle. Un diplôme dans les domaines de la santé, de la pharmacie ou de la chimie sera considéré comme un atout distinctif.

 

  1. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions des paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 de la Section III du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement – édition de Juillet 2016, révisé en Novembre 2020 » relatives aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts, s’applique à la présente manifestation d’intérêt.

 

 

  1. Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection des Consultants Individuels  telle que décrite dans le « Règlement ».

                  

  1. Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse et aux heures suivantes : Unité de Gestion du Projet SWEDD+ BP : 2268 N’Djamena (TCHAD) N° Téléphone : (+235) 22 53 10 56 Courriel : sweddtchad@gmail.com  Sise au Quartier Repos, rue de 30m à côté du Lycée de la Liberté de 7 heures 30 minutes à 15 heures 30 minutes, tous les jours ouvrables et le vendredi de 7 heures 30 minutes à 12 heures.

 

  1. Les CV en langue française doivent être transmis, à l’attention du Coordonnateur National du projet SWEDD+, au plus tard le 31 août 2026 à 15Heures et 30 minutes heure locale (N’Djaména) et porter clairement la mention « Avis de sollicitation de manifestation d’intérêt N°002/MFBEPCI/SE/SG/SWEDD+/PM/2026, relatif au recrutement d’un consultant individuel pour élaborer le manuel de procédure de  Laboratoire National de Contrôle Qualité des Médicaments (LNCQM) ».

 

L'avis et les TDR complets peuvent être consultés dans le site Web du projet : www.sweddchad.org

 

Le Coordonnateur National du projet SWEDD+

 

 

 

YOUSSOUF AWARE NEÏSSA

République Islamique de Mauritanie

Honneur – Fraternité – Justice

 

Ministère des Affaires Economiques et du Développement (MAED)

 

PROJET AUTONOMISATION DES FEMMES ET DIVIDENDE DEMOGRAPHIQUE EN AFRIQUE SUBSAHARIENNE  (SWEDD+)

 

Crédit  N° IDA  7745 MR

 

 

Avis d’Appel d’Offres National (AON)

 

 

AON : 01/CPMP/SWEDD+/2026

 

Acquérir 3 Cliniques Mobiles pour l'organisation des activités

Sanitaires mobiles

 

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République Islamique de Mauritanie a reçu le Credit N° IDA 7745 MR de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement pour financer le Projet de l’Autonomisation des Femmes et le Dividende Démographique en Afrique Subsaharienne  (SWEDD+) et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce don pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché relatif à « Acquérir 3 Cliniques Mobiles pour l'organisation des activités Sanitaires mobiles »

 

  1. Le Ministère des Affaires économiques et du Développement//Projet Autonomisation des Femmes et Dividende Démographique en Afrique Subsaharienne  (SWEDD+) sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour réaliser « Acquérir 3 Cliniques Mobiles pour l'organisation des activités Sanitaires mobiles». 

 

  1. La passation du Marché sera conduite par Appel d‘Offres National Ouvert  (AONO) en accord avec les procédures définies dans le nouveau cadre de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale et au Règlement des marchés pour les emprunteurs de l'IPI datés de juillet 2016, révisé en 2017,  2018, 2020 et 2025.

 

  1. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de l’UGP du SWEDD Adresse :  Ilot ZRC 447, BP : 238, Tel : 00 222 45 25 76 70/00 222 45 25 30 80 Nouakchott- Mauritanie et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres à l’adresse sus mentionnée ci-dessus de 8h à 17 h.
  2. Les exigences en matière de qualifications sont :
    1. Capacité financière

Le Soumissionnaire doit fournir la preuve écrite qu’il satisfait aux exigences ci-après :

  • Avoir réalisé durant les trois dernières années (2023, 2024 et 2025), un chiffre d’affaires annuel moyen égal au moins à Quinze Millions d’Ouguiyas (15.000.000 MRU).
  • Le Soumissionnaire doit joindre à son offre les Etats financiers certifiés des trois dernières années.
  • Fournir une attestation bancaire, certifiant que le soumissionnaire dispose de liquidités et/ou de facilités de crédit net de tout autre engagement, égales au moins à Trois Million Cinq Cent Mille Ouguiyas (3.500.000 MRU).

 

    1. Capacité technique et expérience

Le Soumissionnaire doit prouver, documentation à l’appui, qu’il satisfait aux exigences de capacité technique ci-après :

  • Le soumissionnaire doit prouver, documentation à l’appui, qu’il a exécuté en tant que fournisseur principal, au cours des Cinq (5) dernières années, au moins Un (1) marché similaire (Clinique Mobile : Véhicule tout terrain doté d’équipements médicaux pouvant fonctionner d’une manière autonome et continue à partir d’une source d’énergie adaptée, tels que définis dans les spécifications techniques du présent DAO). A cet effet, le soumissionnaire doit joindre à son offre la liste des marchés exécutés et copie de toute preuve (attestations de bonne exécution ou procès-verbaux de réception sans réserve) montrant qu’il a exécuté lesdits marchés.
  • Fournir une Autorisant du fabricant pour la Clinique mobile (différents équipements médicaux et du Véhicule tout terrain.
  • Le soumissionnaire doit prouver que les équipements médicaux et le véhicule proposés sont des équipements neufs.
  • Le soumissionnaire doit prouver qu’il dispose en Mauritanie d’un Service après-vente pour les composants des équipements médicaux et les pièces détachées du Véhicule tout terrain.
  1. Aucune marge de préférence ne sera applicable.
  2. Le Soumissionnaire doit fournir un calendrier de livraison dument daté et signé, comportant un délai de livraison de Quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours au plus.
  3. Les offres doivent avoir une durée de validité de 90 jours.
  4. Les prix des fournitures doivent être libellés en Hors toutes taxes. Et une Offre fiscale est requise
  5. Les soumissionnaires intéressés peuvent consulter le dossier d’appel d’offres auprès de l’UGP du SWEDD+, Adresse :  Ilot ZRC 447, BP : 238, Tél : 00 222 45 25 76 70/00 222 45 25 30 80 Nouakchott- Mauritanie, ou l’acquérir contre la présentation d’une quittance de versement au Trésor Public d’un montant non remboursable de deux mille (2000) Ouguiyas MRU.
  6.  Les offres devront être soumises au secrétariat de l’UGP du SWEDD+ : Ilot ZRC 447, BP : 238, Tel : 00 222 45 25 76 70/00 222 45 25 30 80 Nouakchott- Mauritanie Nouakchott – Mauritanie au plus tard le 28/09/2026 à 12H00 TU.
  7. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires présents en personne à la salle de réunion de l’UGP du SWEDD+ : Ilot ZRC 447, BP : 238, Tel : 00 222 45 25 76 70/00 222 45 25 30 80 Nouakchott- Mauritanie le 28/09/2026 à 12H00 TU.

 

  1. Les offres doivent comprendre une garantie de l’offre pour un montant de Cent Cinquante Mille Ouguiyas (150 000 MRU). Elle restera valide 28 jours après la date d’expiration de la validité de l’offre.

ESWATINI ELECTRICITY COMPANY

 

 

 

 

Request for Expression of Interest (REOI)

 

Consultancy Services for a battery ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEM (bESS) GRID INTERGRATION AND PLANNING STUDY 

FOR THE ACCELERATING SUSTAINABLE AND CLEAN ENERGY ACCESS TRANSFORMATION IN ESWATINI (ASCENT) PROJECT

Request for Expression of Interest (REOI)

 

Eswatini Electricity Company (EEC)

(Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini)

Consultancy Services for a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Grid Integration and Planning Study

 

First date of publication:           06 August 2026

Country:                                      Kingdom of Eswatini

Name of Project:                        Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Eswatini (ASCENT Eswatini) Project

Sector:                                          Energy Sector

Project ID No.:                            P508960

Reference:                                   SZ-ECC-561947-CS-CQS

Assignment Title:                       Consulting Services for a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Grid Integration and Planning Study

 

 

  1. The Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini (GoKE) has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), the International Development Agency (IDA) and grant funding from the Global Public Good (GPG) Facility, which are all under the World Bank. The received financing is for the purposes of implementing the Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Eswatini (ASCENT Eswatini) Project (P508960) (the Project), with the involvement of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Energy, as set out in the Loan Agreement, Financing Agreement, Grant Agreement and Project Agreements.

 

  1. The EEC now invites Expressions of Interest (EOI) from interested and eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to provide consulting services for a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Grid Integration and Planning Study.

 

  1. The Consultant shall undertake, but not necessarily be limited to the following tasks:

 

      1. Review of the Existing Energy Power System: Conduct a high-level review of the entire EEC transmission network,
      2. BESS Technology Assessment: Evaluate suitable utility-scale BESS technologies,
      3. Assessment of BESS Grid Applications: Analyze the technical role of BESS in the entire EEC transmission network,
      4. Solar PV and BESS Hybrid Assessment: Assess the benefits of co-locating BESS with committed solar PV projects,
      5. Power System Modelling and Impact Studies: Conduct detailed power system modelling, stability studies and network impact analysis to evaluate the combined impact of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS) devices on the EEC grid.
      6. Optimal BESS and FACTS Devices Location and Sizing: Determine optimal siting, sizing and operational configuration of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS),
      7. Inverter Technology Assessment: Evaluate grid-following and grid-forming applications for BESS,
      8. Grid Resilience and Restoration: Assess the potential role of BESS and FACTS devices in enhancing system resilience,
      9. Economic Assessment: Conduct cost-benefit analysis of Bess deployment options, sensitivity analysis on key parameters, estimate total projects costs, assess financial viability of BESS under ownership and commercial models (public utility ownership, IPP/PPP structures and hybrid models),
      10. Environmental and Social Safeguards: Conduct a preliminary environmental and social screening of candidate BESS sites,
      11. Deployment Strategy and Roadmap: Develop a comprehensive and integrated deployment strategy and implementation roadmap for BESS and FACTS technologies.

 

 

  1. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform all the services. The following documents shall also be submitted along with the EOI applications by all the consulting firms including each member of JV firms:
      • Copies of certificates of incorporation/registration of the consulting firms
      • Annual financial records of the firm for the last 5 years
      • Corporate profile of the firm with quality assurance plan, e.g. ISO 9001, information on organizational strength (Organization structure, number of permanent professional staffs and their expertise, qualifications and number of total staff), evidence of availability of licensed power system analysis software, including but not limited to: PSS®E, DIgSILENT Power Factory, ETAP, PSCAD or equivalent software required for execution of the assignment.

 

  1. The qualifications and shortlisting criteria are:
  • At least ten (10) years’ experience in grid planning, stability, storage, or renewable integration studies.
  • At least five (5) relevant assignments in Africa.
  • Demonstrated experience of at least one (1) relevant assignment in BESS integration, including siting, sizing, and grid impact analysis in Africa.
  • Proven experience of at least one (1) relevant assignment in FACTS devices analysis (e.g., STATCOM, SVC) for voltage control and stability in Africa.
  • Prove Experience with utility transmission networks.
  1. The purpose of this EOI is to establish the consultant who has the best qualifications for the assignment and to invite that consultant to submit a technical and financial proposal. All responses shall be assessed for completeness. The following shall be assessed on a Yes/No basis to determine a PASS or FAIL result; ten (10) years’ experience in grid planning, stability, storage, or renewable integration studies, five (5) relevant assignments in grid planning, stability, storage, or renewable integration studies in Africa, demonstrated experience of at least one (1) relevant assignment in BESS integration, including siting, sizing, and grid impact analysis in Africa and proven experience of at least one (1) relevant assignment in FACTS devices analysis (e.g., STATCOM, SVC) for voltage control and stability in Africa and experience with utility transmission networks.

 

The consultant who has attained the highest pass rate result shall be invited to submit a request for proposal based on the following weighted aspect:

  • General corporate experience; [15]
  • Specific experience in BESS planning and integration studies; [25]
  • Power system planning and stability studies experience; [20]
  • FACTS technology assessment and deployment experience; [15]
  • Experience working with electricity utilities; [15]
  • Regional (African) experience. [10]

 

  1. In order to substantiate the aforementioned consulting jobs/contracts, the Consultant shall submit the Completion Certificates or End User Certificate from clients depicting description of services provided. All Completion Certificate or End User Certificates should be in English; Completion Certificates/ End User Certificates in other languages should be translated and notarized. Incomplete Consulting Contracts will not be taken into account and hence will not be evaluated.

 

  1. Consultants may associate with other consultants to enhance their qualifications. For a JV/consortium, the qualifications and experience of the members may be combined to meet the qualification requirements. The Lead Partner shall demonstrate substantial relevant experience and shall be responsible for contract performance. Consortium members may combine qualifications and experience to meet the overall qualification requirements.

 

  1. All submittal from the consulting firms shall be in English language.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.15 to 3.16 of the Seventh edition of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

  1. The Consultant(s) shall be evaluated and shortlisted based on the qualifications, experience and capability. Qualifications and Experience of key personnel will not be evaluated at this stage. The shortlisted consultant will subsequently be invited to submit Technical and Financial Proposals and the Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method as per the Seventh edition of Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2025.

 

  1. Interested eligible consultants may obtain further information by sending an email to the address below or visiting during office hours from 10.00 to 16.00 hrs. The Terms of Reference for the proposed consulting services can be accessed at the link below:

 

https://www.eec.co.sz/electricity/projects/ascent/docs/Battery_Energy_Storage_System_BESS_Grid_Intergration_and_Planning_Study_TORs.pdf

 

 

  1. Expression of interest must be delivered in a written form (in person or by e-mail) to the address below no later than 11h00 SAST on 03 September 2026.

procnotices.notice_text:
“Programa Plan de Inversiones de Transmisión (PIT) - Recuperación Económica Post COVID-19 en el Perú” (Programa PIT)
Decreto de Urgencia N°048-2021


Mediante Decreto de Urgencia N°048-2021, el Gobierno Central autoriza excepcionalmente al MINEM, la formulación, evaluación, ejecución y declaratoria de viabilidad de los Proyectos que forman parte del Programa PIT.
Asimismo, con Decreto Supremo Nº083-2025-EF se modifica el artículo 3 del Decreto Supremo Nº377-2021-EF, respecto a la aprobación de operación de endeudamiento externo con el Banco Internacional de Reconstrucción y Fomento - BIRF prevista en la Ley Nº31086, Ley de Endeudamiento del Sector Público para el Año Fiscal 2021, estableciendo como Unidad Ejecutora: La Unidad Ejecutora del Programa “Plan de Inversiones de Transmisión (PIT)
- Recuperación Económica Post COVID - 19 en Perú” es el Ministerio de Energía y Minas, a través de la Dirección General de Electrificación Rural”.
Motivo por el cual, la DGER propone contratar el siguiente servicio de consultoría individual:

SELECCIÓN DE CONSULTORES INDIVIDUALES N°003-2026- PIT - CONTRATACIÓN DE UN (01) ESPECIALISTA CIVIL PARA EL SOPORTE EN EL SEGUIMIENTO Y SUPERVISIÓN DE LA EJECUCIÓN FÍSICA DE LA OBRA SET MOTIL.

La DGER invita a los Profesionales que cumplan con el perfil y cuenten con la experiencia requerida para cumplir con los objetivos del Programa PIT, por lo cual se les solicita presentar sus expresiones de interés para el presente servicio de consultoría individual.
Para ello, se adjuntan a la presente los Términos de Referencia, los formatos e información a presentar para el SCI N°003-2026-PIT; los cuales también se encuentran en el sitio web:

https://www.gob.pe/65476-programa-plan-de-inversiones-de-transmision-pit-recuperacion-economica-post-covid-19

El Consultor Individual será seleccionado conforme a los procedimientos indicados en los Instrucciones a los Consultores Individuales (SCI).
Las expresiones de interés con los anexos debidamente llenados, la Hoja de vida o Curriculum Vitae (CV); copia de DNI (ambos lados) así como los documentos que sustenten su formación académica y experiencia profesional deberán ser enviados en un único archivo que deberá encontrarse foliado (enumerado) en todas sus páginas, vía correo electrónico a: convocatoriaprogramapit@gmail.com hasta el día 04 de setiembre de 2026.
Es importante indicar que, profesional postulante deberá señalar en el “Asunto” del correo electrónico el SCI N°003-2026-PIT.

PEDIDO DE PROPOSTAS

CONTRATAÇÃO DE SERVIÇOS DE ENTREGA 

Concurso Ref. MZ- MZ-MAEF-563717-NC-RFQ
 

1. O Governo de Moçambique, representado pelo Ministério da Administração Estatal e Função Pública (MAEFP) com o apoio financeiro do Banco Mundial, está a implementar o Projecto de Desenvolvimento Urbano e Descentralização (PDUL) que está a beneficiar 22 Municípios das Províncias de Niassa, Zambézia, Sofala e Gaza. O Objectivo de Desenvolvimento do Projecto é "Fortalecer o desempenho institucional e prover melhores infra-estruturas e serviços às entidades locais participantes e dar uma resposta imediata e eficaz a uma crise ou emergência elegível”

République Islamique de Mauritanie

Ministère des Affaires Economiques et du Développement (MAED)

 

PROJET AUTONOMISATION DES FEMMES ET DIVIDENDE DEMOGRAPHIQUE EN AFRIQUE SUBSAHARIENNE  (SWEDD+)

Acquérir 6 véhicules de transport adaptés pour l'acheminement des produits de santé dans les 6 wilayas
