Le Gouvernement de la République Islamique de Mauritanie a reçu le Credit N° IDA7745 D MR de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement pour financer le Projet de l’Autonomisation des Femmes et le Dividende Démographique en Afrique Subsaharienne  (SWEDD+) et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce don pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché relatif à « Acquérir 6 véhicules de transport adaptés pour l'acheminement des produits de santé dans les 6 wilayas »

 

  1. Le Ministère des Affaires économiques et du Développement//Projet Autonomisation des Femmes et Dividende Démographique en Afrique Subsaharienne  (SWEDD+) sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour réaliser « Acquérir 6 véhicules de transport adaptés pour l'acheminement des produits de santé dans les 6 wilayas». 

 

  1. La passation du Marché sera conduite par Appel d‘Offres National Ouvert  (AONO) en accord avec les procédures définies dans le nouveau cadre de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale et au Règlement des marchés pour les emprunteurs de l'IPI datés de juillet 2016, révisé en 2017,  2018, 2020 et 2025.

 

  1. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de l’UGP du SWEDD Adresse :  Ilot ZRC 447, BP : 238, Tel : 00 222 45 25 76 70/00 222 45 25 30 80 Nouakchott- Mauritanie et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres à l’adresse sus mentionnée ci-dessus de 8h à 17 h.
  2. Les exigences en matière de qualifications sont :
    1. Capacité financière

Le Soumissionnaire doit fournir la preuve écrite qu’il satisfait aux exigences ci-après :

  • Avoir réalisé durant les trois dernières années, un chiffre d’affaires annuel moyen égal au moins à Quinze Millions d’Ouguiyas (15.000.000 MRU).
  • Le Soumissionnaire doit joindre à son offre les Etats financiers certifiés des trois dernières années.
  • Fournir une attestation bancaire, certifiant que le soumissionnaire dispose de liquidités et/ou de facilités de crédit net de tout autre engagement, égales au moins à Trois Million Cinq Cent Mille Ouguiyas (3.500.000 MRU).

 

    1. Capacité technique et expérience

Le Soumissionnaire doit prouver, documentation à l’appui, qu’il satisfait aux exigences de capacité technique ci-après :

  • Le soumissionnaire doit prouver, documentation à l’appui, qu’il a exécuté en tant que fournisseur principal, au cours des Cinq (5) dernières années, au moins Un (1) marché similaire (Véhicule tout terrain frigorifique, tel que défini dans les spécifications techniques du présent DAO). A cet effet, le soumissionnaire doit joindre à son offre la liste des marchés exécutés et copie de toute preuve (attestations de bonne exécution ou procès-verbaux de réception sans réserve) montrant qu’il a exécuté lesdits marchés.
  • Fournir une Autorisant du fabricant pour la Clinique mobile (différents équipements médicaux et du Véhicule tout terrain.
  • Le soumissionnaire doit prouver que les équipements médicaux et le véhicule proposés sont des équipements neufs.
  • Le soumissionnaire doit prouver qu’il dispose en Mauritanie d’un Service après-vente pour les composants des équipements médicaux et les pièces détachées du Véhicule tout terrain.

 

 

  1. Aucune marge de préférence ne sera applicable.
  2. Le Soumissionnaire doit fournir un calendrier de livraison dument daté et signé, comportant un délai de livraison de Quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours au plus.
  3. Les offres doivent avoir une durée de validité de 90 jours.
  4. Les prix des fournitures doivent être libellés en Hors toutes taxes. Et une Offre fiscale est requise
  5.  Les soumissionnaires intéressés peuvent consulter le dossier d’appel d’offres auprès de l’UGP du SWEDD+, Adresse :  Ilot ZRC 447, BP : 238, Tél : 00 222 45 25 76 70/00 222 45 25 30 80 Nouakchott- Mauritanie, ou l’acquérir contre la présentation d’une quittance de versement au Trésor Public d’un montant non remboursable de deux mille (2000) Ouguiyas MRU.
  6. Les offres devront être soumises au secrétariat de l’UGP du SWEDD+ : Ilot ZRC 447, BP : 238, Tel : 00 222 45 25 76 70/00 222 45 25 30 80 Nouakchott- Mauritanie Nouakchott – Mauritanie au plus tard le 28/09/2026 à 12H00 TU.
  7. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires présents en personne à la salle de réunion de l’UGP du SWEDD+ : Ilot ZRC 447, BP : 238, Tel : 00 222 45 25 76 70/00 222 45 25 30 80 Nouakchott- Mauritanie le 28/09/2026 à 12H00 TU.

 

  1. Les offres doivent comprendre une garantie de l’offre pour un montant de Cent Cinquante Mille Ouguiyas (150 000 MRU). Elle restera valide 28 jours après la date d’expiration de la validité de l’offre.

REPUBLIQUE DEMOCRATIQUE DU CONGO

PROJET DE RESILIENCE AUX INONDATIONS URBAINES EN REPUBLIQUE DEMOCRATIQUE DU CONGO « PRIUR »

Recrutement d'un consultant (firme) chargé de contrôle et surveillance des travaux de réhabilitation des voiries et collecteurs de plateau de Kisenso

N° de référence (selon le plan de passation de marche) : ZR-PRIUR-502972-CS-QCBS

Le Gouvernement de la République du Démocratique du Congo a sollicité un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet de Résilience aux Inondations Urbaines en République Démocratique du Congo, PRIUR en sigle, et a l’intention d’affecter une partie du produit à des services de consultant.

Les services de consultant (« les services ») comprennent le contrôle et la surveillance des travaux d’aménagement et de réhabilitation des voiries et collecteurs de plateau de Kisenso sur 2 387,34 ml pour les voiries et 7 963 ml pour les rivières et collecteurs.

Les Termes de Reference (TDR) complets de la mission sont disponibles sur le site de la Cellule Infrastructures, www.celluleinfra.org sous l’onglet « Appel d’Offres ».

Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services. Les critères de sélection d’une liste restreinte sont les suivants : (i) Avoir une existence légale d’au moins dix (10) ans, assortie de documents de base légale et réglementaire y afférente ;  (ii) Avoir réalisé au moins quatre (04) missions de contrôle et surveillance des travaux de génie civil similaires, dont une (01) expérience de contrôle et surveillance des travaux d’aménagement d’une rivière ou de lutte contre les inondations en milieu urbain au cours des dix dernières années ; (iii) Avoir une connaissance des procédures et directives de la Banque mondiale. Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués à l’étape de la préparation de la liste restreinte.

procnotices.notice_text:
FEDERAL REPUBLIC OF NIGERIA

FEDERAL MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES AND SANITATION

SUSTAINABLE POWER AND IRRIGATION FOR NIGERIA(SPIN) PROJECT 

Country: Nigeria

Project ID No: P179684

IDA Credit No: IDA76370

Assignment Title:    CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR DESIGN REVIEW, DETAILED ENGINEERING DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION FOR THE REHABILITATION OF DOMA AND GALALA DAMS IN NASARAWA AND BAUCHI STATES

Reference No.FMWR&S/SPIN/QCBS/CS/2026/19A

The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN), through the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation (FMWRS) is currently implementing the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project  with a credit received from the International Development Association (IDA) and it intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The SPIN Project is designed to strengthen dam safety and improve the management of water resources for hydropower, irrigation, flood management and climate resilience in selected areas of Nigeria. The Federal Government of Nigeria is undertaking the rehabilitation and safety improvement of selected federal dams and associated hydraulic appurtenances, including detailed engineering design, preparation of rehabilitation measures, and construction supervision services to enhance structural integrity, operational reliability, and long-term climate resilience.

The objective of the Assignment:

The overall objective of the assignment is to undertake design review, producing the design and engineering drawings, technical specifications, works requirements, the bill of quantities and construction supervision for the rehabilitation of Doma and Galala Dams and associated hydraulic appurtenances. The Consultant shall review and utilize the findings, conclusions and recommendations of the Dam Safety Review Panel of Experts (DSRPoE) Dam Safety Assessment Reports as the technical basis for the assignment.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the Consultancy Services can be found at the following link Doma and Galala link:https://1drv.ms/w/c/27ae132c0b4b71fe/IQCxiF0AGdCTTbXw4JbJCBu8ARpQuzRETxGxSb678Fq_DUs?e=HGhJcY

The Federal Ministry of Water Resources through its Federal Project Management Unit (FPMU) of the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) project now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Service. Interested firms must provide sufficient and verifiable information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The Short-Listing Criteria are:

  1. Proven evidence of general experience of Consultancy in water resources management, dam engineering and dam safety;

Demonstrated experience of at least ten (10) years in providing consultancy services related to construction supervision and contract administration of infrastructure projects, with relevant experience in areas such as dam engineering, dam safety, rehabilitation and improvement of dams and associated hydraulic structures, detailed engineering design, and construction supervision of water resources infrastructure.

NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                      Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                                  Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Procurement Specialist

No: MW-NLGFC-563881-CS-INDV

                     

                                          Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Procurement Specialist on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Procurement Specialist at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for Procurement Specialist are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The overall objective of the Procurement Specialist is to ensure that all goods, works, consulting services, and non-consulting services required for project implementation are procured efficiently, transparently, economically, and in compliance with applicable procurement regulations and donor requirements.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. Coordinate the preparation and updating of Project’s Annual Procurement Plan;
  2. Prepare the General Procurement Notices (GPN), and Specific Procurement Notices (SPN), and Solicitations of Expression of Interests (SEOI), when required;
  3. Preparation of solicitation Documents such as request For bids, request for proposals and request For quotations for goods for procurement of goods, works, consulting and non-consulting services.
  4. Manage evaluation of bids/proposals/quotations including managing contract negotiation meetings;
  5. Updating the World Bank Procurement Tracking System for monitoring of the Project procurement activities (STEP) for NLGFC and Local Authorities including seeking “No Objection”, from the World Bank for the Procurement Plan and other stages in case of all procurements.
  6. Ensure that STEP is updated and used in real time for the local authorities;
  7. Preparation of evaluation reports, contracts, award notices and other procurement and contractual documents as required;
  8. Establish and maintain procedures for the receiving, inspecting, testing and acceptance of goods;
  9. Ensure compliance with procurement methods and prior review thresholds applicable to the Project;
  10. Ensure all procurement activities are carried out in accordance with the agreed procedures, including the Financing Agreement; the World Bank Procurement Guidelines/regulations; and Government of Malawi Public Procurement and Disposal of Assets Act 2025, where applicable;
  11. Assist in timely payments to suppliers, and consultants and also ensuring their contractual obligations such as payment guarantees, Insurance premiums and performance Bonds;
  12. Establish and Maintain a contract management plan covering all infrastructures, sub components under GESD 2.0 across all participating councils to monitor contractor performance against milestones and advice on contract modifications and claims, including but not limited to variations, extensions, dispute resolutions and completion certificates
  13. Establish and maintain a central procurement filing system, and ensure all related documents are included in the respective files (physically and electronically);
  14. Establish a performance monitoring database for all suppliers and consultants, and ensure timely updates of the system;
  15. Preparation and timely submission Bid Evaluation Repots; and Monthly Procurement Plan Implementation Status Reports for submission to the World Bank.
  16. Preparation and timely submission of monthly, quarterly and annual procurement progress reports for the PIT / Project Coordinator, aligned/coordinated with the work plan, to be submitted to NLGFC and the World Bank task team monthly/quarterly/annually.

4.      Qualifications and Experience

 

The candidate should meet the following qualifications:

 

  1. BSc in Procurement/Supply Chain/Logistics Management; or Bachelor of Business Administration/Management; or Professional Procurement/ Logistic/ Supply Chain Qualification  
  2. Master’s Degree in Procurement/Supply Chain/Logistics; or Master of Business Administration/Management;
  3. A minimum of eight (8) years of experience in procurement management in the public sector;
  4. Working knowledge of the Government of Malawi’s Public Procurement laws, regulations and procedures;
  5. Proven leadership and mentoring skills and evidence of ability to improve procurement performance;
  6. Proven ability to work under tight deadlines, and excellent team skills, including in multi-sectoral teams;
  7. Good computer skills and proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word and PowerPoint, etc.);
  8. Highly motivated and enthusiastic person with excellent planning, analytical, communications and   interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy;
  9. Membership of professional bodies like MIPS or CIPS-UK is considered an asset;
  10. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English;
  11. Proficiency in using computer applications e.g. MS Word, Excel and Power Point; and
  12. Upholding of anticorruption and antibribery ethics.

 

5. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

 

The Contract is for a period of 3 years with yearly review. The renewal of the contract is upon satisfactory appraisal results.

 

6. LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

The Procurement Specialist (Consultant) will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Procurement Specialist (Consultant) will occasionally be required to travel to district authorities in Malawi to engage with procurement teams to guide and improve project implementation as it concerns procurement

7.REPORTING

The Procurement Specialist (Consultant) will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Head of Procurement at NLGFC for all technical matters, and will support local authorities’ Procurement Officers for the GESD 2.0 project.

.

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information including the detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 7:30 hours to 12:00 hours and from 13:00 hours to 16:30 hours except on Weekends and Public Holidays

 

9. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Interested applicants who meet the above requirements should submit application letters together with concise Curriculum Vitae (CV), National ID, and copies of relevant certificates to the address below not later than 17.30 hours on Friday, 11th September 2026.

 

The National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) is committed to diversifying Gender equality in its operations and strongly encourages women to apply for the above vacant position.

recruitment@nlgfc.gov.mw /ed@nlgfc.gov.mw

Only shortlisted applicants will be considered for further assessments.

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

INDIA

STRENGTHENING COASTAL RESILIENCE AND ECONOMY IN THE UNION TERRITORY OF PUDUCHERRY (PY-SHORE)

Environment, Water Resources, Coastal Resilience, Fisheries and Blue Economy

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Loan No.: To be assigned

Project ID No.: P516041

The Government of Puducherry, India intends to apply for financing in the amount of US$ 119.70 equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Strengthening Coastal Resilience and Economy in the Union Territory of Puducherry (PY-SHORE) Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this Project. This Project will be jointly financed by the Government of Puducherry.

The Project will include the following components:

Strengthening Institutional Capacity for Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM): Development and implementation of Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) Plans, Decision Support Systems (DSS), Marine Spatial Planning (MSP), analytical studies, environmental monitoring systems, capacity building and institutional strengthening.

Shoreline Management, Coastal Protection and Conservation: Shoreline management, coastal protection and stabilization measures, Southern Reef construction, nature-based solutions including mangrove restoration, coastal habitat restoration and sand dune rehabilitation, coastal aquifer recharge, Green Cruise Terminal, eco-tourism infrastructure and other coastal resilience investments.

3. Enhancing Livelihoods for Communities Reliant on Natural Resources: Climate resilient coastal fishing villages, modernization of fisheries infrastructure and fishing harbours, sustainable fisheries, eco-tourism development, livelihood enhancement initiatives and other blue economy interventions.

4. Improving Marine Pollution Management and Promoting Plastic Circularity: Interception and diversion of sea-bound wastewater, marine plastics management, fishnet collection and pre-processing centres, Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs), environmental monitoring and other interventions to reduce marine pollution and promote circular economy.

5. Project Management: Establishment and operation of the Project Management Unit (PMU), project management, technical assistance, monitoring and evaluation, procurement, financial management, environmental and social management, communication, stakeholder engagement and institutional coordination.

The Project is expected to include procurement of civil works, goods, non-consulting services and consulting services. Major procurement packages are expected to include coastal protection and environmental infrastructure works, fisheries and tourism infrastructure, laboratory and monitoring equipment, information technology systems, technical assistance and project management consultancy services, consultancy services for preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and other environmental and social instruments, engineering design and supervision, financial management, audit and other specialized consultancy services, as applicable.

Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Current Edition) (Procurement Regulations), and is open to all eligible firms and individuals as defined in the Procurement Regulations. After project negotiations, the World Bank shall arrange the publication on its external website of the agreed initial procurement plan and all subsequent updates once it has provided a no objection.

Specific procurement notices for contracts subject to open international competitive procurement will be announced, as they become available on the World Bank’s external website and on the official website of Government of Puducherry / Puducherry Resilient Infrastructure Development Enterprise Ltd. (https://pwd.py.gov.in) and in at least one newspaper of national circulation in India, as applicable.

procnotices.contact_address: Red Cross House Area 14 Private Bag 352 Lilongwe 3, Malawi
procnotices.contact_organization: National Local Government Finance Committee
procnotices.notice_text:
NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                      Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                               Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Occupational Health and Safety Specialist

No: MW-NLGFC-563903-CS-INDIV

                     

                                         Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

 

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Occupational Health and Safety Specialist on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of Occupational Health and Safety Specialist tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for Occupational Health and Safety Specialist are as follows:

 

The Objectives of the Assignment

The main aim of this assignment is to ensure that all OHS risks and impacts are managed in accordance with national Occupational Health and Safety Policies and framework, World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), and Good International Industry Practice (GIIP). Working with other team members, the Occupational Health and Safety Specialist will ensure the implementation of the project’s occupational health and safety safeguards instruments, monitor compliance by project implementers and report progress in all the 28 district and 4 municipal local authorities.

3. Duties and Responsibilities

 

The duties will include but will not be limited to:

 

  1. Considering World Bank Environmental Health Safety Guidelines (EHSG), Good International Industry Practice (GIIP), compile OHS procedures update where applicable the OHS strategy, system and the operational plans for the district led subcomponent which falls under the National Local Government Finance Committee PIU;
  2. Together with OHS officers of contractors, develop, update, coordinate and facilitate the development and/or revision of and OHS risk assessments and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for the various activities under the applicable activities of the Project;
  3. Liaise with other specialists (including Environmental, Social, Project Engineer, etc.) in the team on OHS matters to review severe OHS incidents, recurring minor incidents, and near misses that have occurred on project with the aim to further mitigate these from repeating;
  4. Facilitate the development of Health and Safety Manual and a health and Safety Management plan for the local authorities implemented project activities and incorporate the relevant OHS measures (including emergency preparedness and response measures) into the Labour Management Procedures (LMP) and community Safety;
  5. Conducting Occupational Health Safety site inspections on a regular basis with adequate frequency;
  6. Identify potential hazards to project workers and community members;
  7. Ensure preventive and protective measures, including modification, substitution, or elimination of hazardous conditions or substances;
  8. Ensure applicable protective equipment to protect against residual risks is provided;
  9. Providing internal audits on Occupational Health and Safety issues all project sites implemented by local authorities;
  10. Facilitating wellness health awareness and screening Programs in all the local authorities;
  11. Ensure training requirements for project workers, and where necessary community members, are included, and training records are maintained;
  12. Support project teams and clients in investigating the root cause/s of the incidents and developing appropriate remedial and mitigation measures;
  13. Prepare and deliver reports to the project on OHS incidents, patterns of incidents, and proposed recommendations;
  14. Develop and implement a comprehensive intervention to improve worker OHS, and Community Health and Safety for communities directly impacted by the project;
  15. Develop and implement a training program on Occupational Health and Safety for local authorities and contractors; and maintain training records;
  16. Document and report occupational accidents, diseases and incidents;
  17. Recommend measures to help protect workers, and community members, from potentially hazardous work methods, working at heights, scaffolding measures, working adjacent to flowing water, hazardous substances and waste management and disposal, and other relevant processes, or materials;
  18. Advise communities and/or institutions/local authorities regarding health or safety issues;
  19. Inspect or evaluate workplace environments, equipment, or practices to ensure compliance with safety standards and government regulations;
  20. Develop or maintain hygiene programs, such as noise surveys, continuous atmosphere monitoring, ventilation surveys, or asbestos management plans;
  21. Document and report on job hazard assessments, identified mitigation measures, permits to work, standard operating procedures developed to carry out work safely based on Job Hazard Assessment (JHA) and Permission To Work (PTW), all incidents or near misses, use of first aid kits, tool box talks, training programme for workers, labour procedures, signed codes of conduct by all persons working on or visiting the site, contracts of all workers, activity ESMP, Contractors ESMP, any permits for the work or resources used for the work, etc.;
  22. Describe emergency prevention and preparedness and response arrangements to emergency situations, and report significant incidents to the LG PIU and World Bank within 48 hours;
  23. Review and inputs into community emergency procedure plans for subcomponent activities;
  24. Propose remedies for adverse impacts such as occupational injuries, deaths, disability and disease;
  25. Inspect work environments to ensure safety for the workers and community in all project sites;
  26. Conduct safety training or education programs, job hazard assessments, and demonstrate the use of safety equipment, and maintain training records;
  27. Investigate health-related complaints and inspect facilities to ensure that they comply with public health legislation and regulations, and World Bank’s ESF and ESHS requirements, and project ESMF;
  28. Develop or maintain medical monitoring programs for employees and contractors;
  29. Set up monitoring systems for the sites, including file management on site for Toolbox talks and topics, ongoing skills and training development, SOPs, permits to work, incident reports, monitoring First Aid kits, etc. Ensuring first aid kits are appropriately stocked to type of activities anticipated on sites, etc;
  30. Develop and review and monitoring emergency procedures for sites including ensuring correct fire prevent controls and training in place, etc;
  31. Coordinate “right-to-know” programs regarding hazardous chemicals or other substances, and safety procedure;
  32. Maintain or update Emergency Response Plans or procedures, as well as waste management plan, traffic safety management plan, hazardous substances management plan, etc., with necessary SOPs or safety procedures developed in the OHS strategy and plan; and
  33. Apply ESS4 to anticipate and avoid adverse impacts on the health and safety of project-affected communities during the project life cycle from both routine and non-routine circumstances, including to avoid or minimize community expose to project-related traffic and road safety risks, diseases and hazardous materials, effective measures to address emergency events, and ensure safeguarding of personnel and property is carried out in a manner that avoids or minimizes risks to the project affected communities.

4.      Qualifications and Experience

 

The candidate should meet the following qualifications:

 

  1. Master’s Degree in disciplines such as Engineering (Civil, Electrical, Environmental, Quality and Safety), Environmental Health and Safety.
  2. A qualification and or international certificate in OHS such as NEBOSH, or similar.
  3. A minimum of 8 years of relevant working experience in developing, implementing and/or supervising OHS in construction, with experience in transport infrastructure, energy, hydropower, DRM and or extractives sectors.
  4. Knowledge of OHS management systems, including experience auditing/ assessing health and safety programs and systems.
  5. Membership of professional bodies and experience in implementing World Bank funded projects and/or other multilateral banks’ OHS policies will be an added advantage.
  6. Demonstrated ability to assess technical issues of occupational health and safety and to effect a cultural change to create a culture of safety across a workplace or organization
  7. Have excellent oral and written communication skills in English, as well as team participation and management skills
  8. Proficiency in using computer applications e.g. MS Word, Excel and Power Point.

 

5. DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

6. LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

 

The OHS Specialist will be based at the National Local Government Finance Committee Head Office in Lilongwe. The OHS Specialist will be required to travel to district authorities and to project sites in Malawi to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation.

7.REPORTING

The Occupational Health and Safety Specialist will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Director of Social Economic Services at the NLGFC for technical matters and will work in collaboration with local authorities and other specialists under the project; Environmental Safeguards Specialist, Social Safeguards Specialist, and Project Engineers.

.

8.MODE OF APPLICATION

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14. 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations of IPF Borrowers” dated September, 2025 (“Procurement regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant (INDV) selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information including the detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 7:30 hours to 12:00 hours and from 13:00 hours to 16:30 hours except on Weekends and Public Holidays

 

9.SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Interested applicants who meet the above requirements should submit application letters together with concise Curriculum Vitae (CV), National ID, and copies of relevant certificates to the address below not later than 17.30 hours on Friday, 11th September 2026.

The National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) is committed to diversifying Gender equality in its operations and strongly encourages women to apply for the above vacant position.

 

 

 

The Executive Director

National Local Government Finance Committee

Area 14, Red Cross Building

Presidential Way

P.O Box 31162

Lilongwe 3

Or through the following email address:

recruitment@nlgfc.gov.mw/ ed@nlgfc.gov.mw

Only shortlisted applicants will be considered for further assessments.

Request for Expressions of Interest

(Consulting Services – Firm Selection)

People’s Republic of China

World Bank-financed China: Emerging Infectious Diseases Prevention, Preparedness and Response Project – Hainan Province
(Global “One Health” Hainan Demonstration Project)

Loan No.: 9084-CN

Procurement No.: 0733-26093994

Assignment Title: Design for the Renovation of the One Health International Research Institute Platform and the Upgrading and Renovation of Key Laboratories

Contract No.: HN-FC-93

The Government of the People’s Republic of China has received a loan from the World Bank to finance the China: Emerging Infectious Diseases Prevention, Preparedness and Response Project – Hainan Province (Global “One Health” Hainan Demonstration Project) and intends to apply part of the proceeds to consulting services.

The main scope of this consulting service (hereinafter referred to as the “Service”) includes the renovation of the public platform of the One Health International Research Institute and the upgrading and renovation of the One Health Key Laboratory. The assignment involves two renovation projects at Hainan University, namely the One Health International Research Institute and the One Health Key Laboratory. The demonstrated area for unfinished interior renovation is 11,236.04 m², including a 2,600 m² enhanced intelligent biosafety integrated platform laboratory. The renovation area is 8,854.29 m², with a total area of 20,090.33 m². The final area shall be subject to the actual area determined in the construction design. The deliverables of the Service shall also comply with Hainan University’s procedures for the construction of professional laboratories and site entry for renovation works.

The consulting service will cover the preparation of the preliminary design and cost estimate, detailed construction drawings, project budget, and bills of quantities (including quantities of works, equipment, etc.), providing the design and cost basis for the subsequent construction of the public platform of the One Health International Research Institute and the upgrading and renovation of the One Health Key Laboratory. Further details are provided in the Terms of Reference (TOR).

The estimated total level of effort for this consulting service is 24 person-months, and the expected implementation period is 3 months from the date the contract is signed and becomes effective.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for this consulting service are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

Hainan University (hereinafter referred to as the “Client”) now invites eligible consulting firms (the “Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the above-mentioned consulting services. Interested Consultants shall provide the relevant supporting documents in accordance with the following requirements. The Expression of Interest (i.e., the bid submission) shall include, at a minimum, the following:

  1. A brief introduction to the Consultant, including its organizational structure, staffing, etc.
  2. Letter of Authorization, identification documents of the legal representative and the authorized representative. If the Consultant is a joint venture, a Joint Venture Agreement shall also be provided (in a format determined by the Consultant).
  3. A copy of the Consultant’s valid business license or Certificate of Legal Person of a Public Institution.
  4. If the Consultant is a state-owned enterprise or public institution, it shall provide its articles of association and the audited financial audit report and financial statements for 2025 (including, at a minimum, the balance sheet, cash flow statement, and income statement/profit and loss statement), or equivalent alternative supporting documents, such as the 2025 internal financial statements of the institution or the final accounts report approved by the competent higher-level authority.
  5. The Consultant shall possess a Class A qualification for engineering design in the Architectural Industry (Construction Engineering) and shall be capable of preparing design documents for renovation projects and technical specifications for procured equipment, as well as undertaking all engineering design and related design services required for the project. A copy of the valid Class A qualification certificate for engineering design in the Architectural Industry (Construction Engineering) shall be provided as evidence.

  6. The Consultant shall possess the relevant capabilities and/or experience necessary to perform the contract:

    During the past five years (from June 1, 2021 to the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest), the Consultant shall have completed at least three architectural engineering design projects, with the contract value of each project being not less than CNY 800,000. Relevant supporting documents for the project experience shall be provided. The supporting documents shall include, at a minimum, copies of the key pages of the contracts (which shall clearly indicate key information such as the name of the entity, scope of services, contract value, and contract signing date) and proof of project completion, such as a project completion acceptance report/certificate, a completion confirmation letter issued by the client and bearing the official seal of the client, or a signed receipt for the approved project design drawings or an approval certificate confirming that the design has passed review.

  7. The Consultant shall have a good track record and reputation and shall provide a screenshot of the search results from the Credit China website showing that it has no record of violations. The screenshot shall include, at a minimum, the search record for the “List of Parties Subject to Serious Violations of Trust in Government Procurement”.
  8. Any other documents that the Consultant considers necessary to provide, if applicable.

At this stage, the Consultants will not be evaluated or ranked. The Client will select one firm with the best qualifications and relevant experience from among all Consultants that have submitted Expressions of Interest and invite the selected firm to submit its Technical and Financial Proposals and proceed with negotiations.

Interested Consultants should take note of the provisions of Sections 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing (IPF) – Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services (November 2020 edition), which set forth the World Bank’s policy on conflicts of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms when submitting their Expressions of Interest to enhance their qualifications, but they shall clearly indicate whether such association is in the form of a Joint Venture and/or Subconsultancy. If a Joint Venture is formed, all members of the Joint Venture shall meet the “Qualification Requirements for Consultants” specified in this Request for Expressions of Interest. If a Joint Venture is selected, all members of the Joint Venture, together with its subconsultants, shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract.

REPUBLIQUE DU NIGER

PROJET D’APPUI AU DEVELOPPEMENT DES CULTURES IRRIGUEES ET A L’INTENSIFICATION DE LA PRODUCTION ANIMALE (PACIPA)

***********

UNITE DE GESTION DE PROJET

 

Demande de Cotation Ouverte No0032/2026/TRVX/PACIPA(NE-LAMP-551787-CW-RFQ) relatif aux travaux de construction et opérationnalisation de deux (2) unités d'azote liquide à Tahoua et Zinder.

  1. Cet Avis d’appel d’offres fait suite à la publication de l’Avis Général de Passation des Marchés (AGPM) publié sur le site de la Banque Mondiale le 05 Août 2025 et sur le Sahel Dimanche du 08 Août 2025.
  2. Le Gouvernement du Niger a sollicité et obtenu de la Banque Mondiale (IDA) le financement du Projet d’Appui au développement des Cultures Irriguées et à l’Intensification de la Production Animale (PACIPA). Il se propose d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour réaliser les travaux de construction et opérationnalisation de deux (2) unités d'azote liquide à Tahoua et Zinder.

Le délai d’exécution est de trois (3) mois à compter de l’ordre de service à démarrer les travaux.

  1. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet (UGP) sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises (voir critères de qualification dans le dossier de cotation).
  2. La procédure sera conduite par mise en concurrence nationale en recourant à une Demande de Cotations (DC) telle que définie dans les Règles de Passation de Marchés applicables aux Emprunteurs dans le cadre de financement de projets d’investissement, en date de Juillet 2016 révisé en septembre 2025 disponible sur www.worldbank.org ;
  3. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir un complément d’informations et consulter gratuitement le Dossier de Cotation en français auprès du Projet d’Appui au développement des Cultures Irriguées et à l’Intensification de la Production Animale (PACIPA), Sis au quartier Koira Kano, Rue KK 41, E-mail : pacipa@pacipa.ne; spm@pacipa.ne; apm@pacipa.ne tous les jours ouvrables du lundi au jeudi de 9 h 00 mn à 17h00, heure locale et le vendredi de 9h00 mn à 12h00 heure locale.
  4. Le Dossier de cotation en français peut être acheté par tout Soumissionnaire intéressé en formulant une demande à l’adresse ci-dessous contre un paiement non remboursable de Vingt Mille (20 000) francs CFA. La méthode de paiement sera en espèces.
  5. L’offre restera valable cent vingt (120) jours à compter de la date d’ouverture des plis.
  6. Les offres en un original et deux (2) copies devront être remises à l’adresse ci-dessous au plus tard le 08 Septembre 2026 à 10h00 mn. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les offres seront ouvertes en présence des soumissionnaires ou leurs représentants à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous à 10h30 minutes.  
  7. L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence ci-dessus est la suivante : Projet d’Appui au développement des Cultures Irriguées et à l’Intensification de la Production Animale (PACIPA), Sis au quartier Koira Kano, Rue KK 41, Tél (227) 20 35 00 68/96 35 56 60, BP : 507 Niamey (Niger).

procnotices.notice_text:
Invitation to Bid for the Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Northern Mindanao and CARAGA (Region 10 and Region 13)

 

1) The Government of the Philippines (GOP) has received a Loan from the World Bank toward the cost of Philippine Digital Infrastructure Project (PDIP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Loan to payments under the contract for the Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Northern Mindanao and CARAGA (Region 10 and Region 13).

2) The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) now invites bids for the Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Northern Mindanao and CARAGA (Region 10 and Region 13) with Estimated Project Cost (EPC) in the amount of Three Hundred Million Seven Hundred Forty-Seven Thousand and Three Hundred Seventy-Two Pesos (PHP 300,747,372.00). Completion of the Works is required within Three Hundred Calendar Days (300 CD) upon receipt of the Notice to Proceed. Bidders shall present evidence of a similar Work Contracts within the last five (5) years prior to the deadline of the submission of bids with a project value amounting to at least fifty percent (50%) of the estimated cost. The description of an eligible bidder is contained in the Bidding Documents, particularly, in Section 5 of the Instructions to Bidders, and Sub-sections 5.2 and 5.4 of the Bid Data Sheet.

3) This package is one of four (4) Middle Mile Level 1 packages being procured separately by the DICT:

a. Regional Cluster 1 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Northern Mindanao and CARAGA (Region 10 and Region 13), PH-DICT-562651-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 300,747,372.00;

b. Regional Cluster 2 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Davao and SOCCSKSARGEN Mindanao (Regions 11 and 12), PH-DICT-562839-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 431,793,643.00;

c. Regional Cluster 3 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Zamboanga Peninsula and Northern Mindanao (Regions 9 and BARMM), PH-DICT-562841-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 519,159,934.00;

d. Regional Cluster 4 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Western, Central, Eastern & Negros Island Visayas (Regions 6, 7, 8 and NIR) of the National Broadband Program, PH-DICT-562842-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 491,959,375.00.

A Bidder may submit a bid for one or more of these packages. Where a Bidder submits bids for more than one package, the minimum Average Annual Turnover and Liquidity required of that Bidder is the sum of the amounts required for all packages for which it submits a bid, and the Bidder shall submit the Declaration of Multi-Package Bidding required under Sub-section 5.4 (iii) of the Bid Data Sheet.

4) Bidding will be conducted in accordance with relevant procedures for open competitive bidding as specified in the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act (RA) 12009, otherwise known as the “New Government Procurement Act”, with some amendments, as stated in the Bidding Documents and is open to all Bidders from eligible source countries, as defined in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. The contract shall be awarded to the Bidder that met the criteria indicated in the Bidding Documents.

5) Interested bidders may obtain further information from the DICT and inspect the Bidding Documents at the address given below from Monday to Thursday, at 8:00 am to 6:00 pm.

6) A complete set of Bidding Documents may be acquired by interested bidders on 21 August 2026 from the address below and upon payment of the Bidding Documents fee of Ten Thousand Pesos (PhP 10,000.00)[1].

It may also be downloaded from the Modernized Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (mPhilGEPS) and the website of the Procuring Entity, provided that bidders shall pay the said Bidding Documents fee not later than the submission of their bids.

A. Department of Information and Communications Technology

BAC Secretariat Office, 19th Floor, DICT Headquarters Studio 7, 807 EDSA, Diliman, Quezon City, 1103 Metro Manila

Website: www.dict.gov.ph

B. e-Procurement System Website

7) The DICT will hold a Pre-Bid Conference on 02 September 2026, 10:00 A.M. Manila Time  at the DICT Procurement Service, 19th Floor, DICT Headquarters, Studio 7, 807 Epifanio de los Santos Avenue, Diliman, Quezon City, 1103 Metro Manila and through video conferencing via Google Meet Platform and/or any other online video conferencing facilities, which shall be open to prospective bidders. All prospective bidders are advised to contact the BAC Secretariat through email at bac.secretariat@dict.gov.ph or landline no. (02) 8-920-01-01 loc. 6108, in advance or prior to the scheduled procurement activity, to get log-in details for the Google Meet.

8) Bids must be duly received by the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) Secretariat through manual submission and upon presentation of the official receipt as proof of payment of the bid documents fee at the address indicated below on or before 14 September 2026, 9:00 A.M. Manila time.  Late bids shall not be accepted.

Bid proposals may be submitted by authorized representatives of the bidder or through courier. Interested bidders that submit bids through courier must make sure that the bid document fees are paid and the copy of the official receipt be submitted to the BAC Secretariat through bac.secretariat@dict.gov.ph or on or before the deadline of submission of bids. Bidding documents fee may be paid through the following:

a. Cash at the office address indicated below;

b. Bank Transfer (For account details, please contact the BAC Secretariat); or

c. Other modes of payment through the DICT eProcurement system which may be accessed at https://eprocurement.dict.gov.ph.

For submission of bids through courier service, bidders are reminded that the courier service personnel must submit the bid proposal to a personnel of the BAC Secretariat Division at the office address provided below. Bid submission/proposal left by the courier service personnel at the lobby guard or any other personnel or staff aside from the authorized BAC Secretariat personnel will not be considered “submitted” for purposes of bid opening. The responsibility to ensure that the courier service personnel submit the bid proposal to the authorized BAC Secretariat personnel is the sole responsibility of the prospective bidder.

Manila time at the DICT Procurement Service, 19th Floor, DICT Headquarters, Studio 7, 807 Epifanio de los Santos Avenue, Diliman, Quezon City, 1103 Metro Manila and through video conferencing via Google Meet Platform and/or any other online video conferencing facilities.

Bids will be opened in the presence of the Bidders’ representatives who choose to attend the activity.

10)  The award criteria for this project shall be Lowest Calculated Responsive Bid (LCRB).

11)  The DICT reserves the right to reject any and all bids, declare a failure of bidding, or not award the contract at any time prior to contract award in accordance with Section 70 of R.A. No. 12009, without thereby incurring any liability to the affected bidder or bidders.

1. O Governo de Moçambique, representado pelo Ministério da Administração Estatal e Função Pública (MAEFP) com o apoio financeiro do Banco Mundial, está a implementar o Projecto de Desenvolvimento Urbano e Descentralização (PDUL) que esta a beneficiar 22 Municípios das Províncias de Niassa, Zambézia, Sofala e Gaza. O Objectivo de Desenvolvimento do Projecto é "Fortalecer o desempenho institucional e prover melhores infra-estruturas e serviços às entidades locais participantes e dar uma resposta imediata e eficaz a uma crise ou emergência elegível”

Lot 4: Serviços de Aluguer de Viaturas Municipios de Zambezia

Lot 5: Serviços de Aluguer de Viaturas Municipios de Niassa

procnotices.notice_text:
Invitation to Bid for the Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Zamboanga Peninsula and Northern Mindanao (Regions 9 and BARMM)


1) The Government of the Philippines (GOP) has received a Loan from the World Bank toward the cost of Philippine Digital Infrastructure Project (PDIP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Loan to payments under the contract for the Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Zamboanga Peninsula and Northern Mindanao (Regions 9 and BARMM).

2) The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) now invites bids for the Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Zamboanga Peninsula and Northern Mindanao (Regions 9 and BARMM) with Estimated Project Cost (EPC) in the amount of Five Hundred Nineteen Million One Hundred Fifty-Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Thirty-Four Pesos Only (519,159,934.00). Completion of the Works is required within Three Hundred Sixty Five (365) calendar days upon receipt of the Notice to Proceed. Bidders shall present evidence of a similar Work Contracts within the last five (5) years prior to the deadline of the submission of bids with a project value amounting to at least fifty percent (50%) of the estimated cost. The description of an eligible bidder is contained in the Bidding Documents, particularly, in Section 5 of the Instructions to Bidders, and Sub-sections 5.2 and 5.4 of the Bid Data Sheet.

3) This package is one of four (4) Middle Mile Level 1 packages being procured separately by the DICT:
a. Regional Cluster 1 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Northern Mindanao and CARAGA (Region 10 and Region 13), PH-DICT-562651-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 300,747,372.00;
b. Regional Cluster 2 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Davao and SOCCSKSARGEN Mindanao (Regions 11 and 12), PH-DICT-562839-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 431,793,643.00;
c. Regional Cluster 3 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Zamboanga Peninsula and Northern Mindanao (Regions 9 and BARMM), PH-DICT-562841-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 519,159,934.00;
d. Regional Cluster 4 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Western, Central, Eastern & Negros Island Visayas (Regions 6, 7, 8 and NIR) of the National Broadband Program, PH-DICT-562842-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 491,959,375.00.

A Bidder may submit a bid for one or more of these packages. Where a Bidder submits bids for more than one package, the minimum Average Annual Turnover and Liquidity required of that Bidder is the sum of the amounts required for all packages for which it submits a bid, and the Bidder shall submit the Declaration of Multi-Package Bidding required under Sub-section 5.4 (iii) of the Bid Data Sheet.

4) Bidding will be conducted in accordance with relevant procedures for open competitive bidding as specified in the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act (RA) 12009, otherwise known as the “New Government Procurement Act”, with some amendments, as stated in the Bidding Documents and is open to all Bidders from eligible source countries, as defined in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. The contract shall be awarded to the Bidder that met the criteria indicated in the Bidding Documents.

5) Interested bidders may obtain further information from the DICT and inspect the Bidding Documents at the address given below from Monday to Thursday, at 8:00 am to 6:00 pm.

6) A complete set of Bidding Documents may be acquired by interested bidders on 21 August 2026 from the address below and upon payment of the Bidding Documents fee of Ten Thousand Pesos (PhP 10,000.00)

It may also be downloaded from the Modernized Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (mPhilGEPS) and the website of the Procuring Entity, provided that bidders shall pay the said Bidding Documents fee not later than the submission of their bids.

Bid proposals may be submitted by authorized representatives of the bidder or through courier. Invitation to Bid for the Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Western, Central, Eastern & Negros Island Visayas (Regions 6, 7, 8 and NIR) of the National Broadband Program


1) The Government of the Philippines (GOP) has received a Loan from the World Bank toward the cost of Philippine Digital Infrastructure Project (PDIP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Loan to payments under the contract for the Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Western, Central, Eastern & Negros Island Visayas (Regions 6, 7, 8 and NIR) of the National Broadband Program.

2) The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) now invites bids for the Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Western, Central, Eastern & Negros Island Visayas (Regions 6, 7, 8 and NIR) of the National Broadband Program with Estimated Project Cost (EPC) in the amount of Four Hundred Ninety-One Million Nine Hundred Fifty-Nine Thousand Three Hundred Seventy-Five Pesos Only (491,959,375.00). Completion of the Works is required within Four hundred twenty (420) calendar days upon receipt of the Notice to Proceed. Bidders shall present evidence of a similar Work Contracts within the last five (5) years prior to the deadline of the submission of bids with a project value amounting to at least fifty percent (50%) of the estimated cost. The description of an eligible bidder is contained in the Bidding Documents, particularly, in Section 5 of the Instructions to Bidders, and Sub-sections 5.2 and 5.4 of the Bid Data Sheet.

3) This package is one of four (4) Middle Mile Level 1 packages being procured separately by the DICT:

a. Regional Cluster 1 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Northern Mindanao and CARAGA (Region 10 and Region 13), PH-DICT-562651-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 300,747,372.00;
b. Regional Cluster 2 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Davao and SOCCSKSARGEN Mindanao (Regions 11 and 12), PH-DICT-562839-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 431,793,643.00;
c. Regional Cluster 3 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Zamboanga Peninsula and Northern Mindanao (Regions 9 and BARMM), PH-DICT-562841-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 519,159,934.00;
d. Regional Cluster 4 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Western, Central, Eastern & Negros Island Visayas (Regions 6, 7, 8 and NIR) of the National Broadband Program, PH-DICT-562842-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 491,959,375.00.

A Bidder may submit a bid for one or more of these packages. Where a Bidder submits bids for more than one package, the minimum Average Annual Turnover and Liquidity required of that Bidder is the sum of the amounts required for all packages for which it submits a bid, and the Bidder shall submit the Declaration of Multi-Package Bidding required under Sub-section 5.4 (iii) of the Bid Data Sheet.

4) Bidding will be conducted in accordance with relevant procedures for open competitive bidding as specified in the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act (RA) 12009, otherwise known as the “New Government Procurement Act”, with some amendments, as stated in the Bidding Documents and is open to all Bidders from eligible source countries, as defined in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. The contract shall be awarded to the Bidder that met the criteria indicated in the Bidding Documents.

5) Interested bidders may obtain further information from the DICT and inspect the Bidding Documents at the address given below from Monday to Thursday, at 8:00 am to 6:00 pm.

6) A complete set of Bidding Documents may be acquired by interested bidders on 21 August 2026 from the address below and upon payment of the Bidding Documents fee of Ten Thousand Pesos (PhP 10,000.00)1.
It may also be downloaded from the Modernized Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (mPhilGEPS) and the website of the Procuring Entity, provided that bidders shall pay the said Bidding Documents fee not later than the submission of their bids.

Bid proposals may be submitted by authorized representatives of the bidder or through courier. Interested bidders that submit bids through courier must make sure that the bid document fee is paid and the copy of the official receipt be submitted to the BAC Secretariat through bac.secretariat@dict.gov.ph or on or before the deadline of submission of bids. Bidding documents fee may be paid through the following:

For submission of bids through courier service, bidders are reminded that the courier service personnel must submit the bid proposal to a personnel of the BAC Secretariat Division at the office address provided below. procnotices.notice_text:
WEST AFRICAN POWER POOL

Project:  WAPP GHANA-CÔTE D’IVOIRE INTERCONNECTION REINFORCEMENT PROJECT

NOTICE OF INTERNATIONAL RECRUITMENT

Revised 23.8.2026

Consultant Services

Selection of individual consultant

Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer

Financing: World Bank IDA

Don IDA No: E4040

Reference: BJ-WAPP-568960-CS-INDV

Open to: All eligible individuals

Duty Station: Abomey-Calavi, Benin

Application Deadline: 24 September 2024

 

  1. CONTEXT

The West African Power Pool (WAPP) was created by the highest decision-making authority of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) at the Conference of Heads of State and Government of the Member States held in Lomé, in December 1999. The Headquarters of the WAPP Secretariat is in Abomey-Calavi, Republic of Benin.

The ECOWAS strategic objective being implemented by the West African Power Pool (WAPP) is based on a dynamic vision of integrating national power grids into a unified regional electricity market, so that such a mechanism would, over the medium and long term, ensure to the ECOWAS citizens access to adequate power quality at an affordable price, and enhance the economic development of the Member States including industrialization growth, Health and Education improvement, Poverty Reduction, various Employment Opportunities Creation, etc…

To achieve its vision of operationalizing a unified ECOWAS regional electricity market, the WAPP Information and Coordination Centre (WAPP ICC), a Department within the WAPP Secretariat has been designated to perform the functions of a System Market Operator (SMO) responsible for coordinating the reliability of the WAPP Interconnected Transmission System (WAPPITS) made up of the power systems of fourteen (14) ECOWAS Member Countries and administration of the regional electricity market.

To this end, the WAPP Secretariat with the support of the World Bank within the Project “WAPP Côte d’Ivoire Interconnection and operationalization of the ECOWAS Regional Electricity Market” intends to reinforce staffing of the ICC Department by filling a key vacant position, that of a Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer

The Engineer will be selected competitively, and the successful candidates will be joining the current team in the Information and Coordination Centre (ICC) as it prepares to operationalize the ECOWAS Regional Electricity Market.

2. ROLE OVERVIEW

Under the supervision of the Head of the System Operations Coordination Division, the Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer is responsible for the management of the ICC's Power System Database. He/She extracts data from various sources (APIs, HIVE tables, and other structured and unstructured data sources) to process and store large volumes of data, ensuring their accuracy, consistency and security. He/She develops reporting dashboards and analytical tools to support the analysis of power system operations, and supports the design, testing and implementation of models and databases for all systems requiring the WAPP Network Model.

The detailed Job description for the assignment may be consulted and/or downloaded from the WAPP website at: www.ecowapp.org/en/tenders

The WAPP General Secretariat invites eligible Individual Consultants to express their interest in providing the required Services described in the Job decription. Interested Consultants must provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services by submitting: (a) a cover letter/motivation letter, and (b) an up-to-date detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV).

WAPP is an equal opportunity employer that offers equal chances to men and women. Qualified women are strongly encouraged to apply.  

3. LANGUAGE

Good oral and written communication skills in English and French  

4. DURATION OF MISSION

The successful candidate shall be offered an initial Consultancy Contract of approximatively 17 months from the beginning of the assignment ( i.e.until April 30, 2028). Upon completion of the World Bank funding, the position shall be absorbed by WAPP.

The beginning of the assignment is planned for November 2026

5. SELECTION METHOD

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the method of "Selection of Individual Consultants" described in the World Bank "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (edition September 2025).  

6. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Applications must be submitted exclusively by email and should bear the subject line: “Application for ICC Engineer- Reference: BJ-WAPP-568960-CS-INDV”.

Paper applications will not be accepted.

Applications may be submitted in either French or English and should be sent to: procurement@ecowapp.org

 Particular emphasis should be placed on references for relevant similar assignments previously carried out, which should be clearly highlighted and described.

Deadline for submission of applications:  September 24, 2026, at noon, 12:00 pm, Benin local time (GMT+1).

Further information may be obtained by sending an email to:

spos@ecowapp.org

With copies to:

cpm@ecowapp.org

 hdhra@ecowapp.org

Only shortlisted candidates shall be contacted for the next stage of the recruitment process.

procnotices.project_name: Philippines Digital Infrastructure Project
procnotices.bid_description: Regional Cluster No. 2: Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Southern and Western Mindanao (Region 11 and Region 12)
procnotices.contact_address: DICT 19th Floor, DICT Headquarters Studio 7, 807 EDSA, Diliman, Quezon City
procnotices.contact_organization: Department of Information and Communications Technology
procnotices.notice_text:
Invitation to Bid for the Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Davao and SOCCSKSARGEN Mindanao (Regions 11 and 12)


1) The Government of the Philippines (GOP) has received a Loan from the World Bank toward the cost of Philippine Digital Infrastructure Project (PDIP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Loan to payments under the contract for the Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Davao and SOCCSKSARGEN Mindanao (Regions 11 and 12).

2) The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) now invites bids for the Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Davao and SOCCSKSARGEN Mindanao (Regions 11 and 12) with Estimated Project Cost (EPC) in the amount of Four Hundred Thirty-One Million Seven Hundred Ninety-Three Thousand Six Hundred Forty-Three Pesos Only (Php 431,793,643.00). Completion of the Works is required within Three Hundred Calendar Days (300 CD) upon receipt of the Notice to Proceed. Bidders shall present evidence of a similar Work Contracts within the last five (5) years prior to the deadline of the submission of bids with a project value amounting to at least fifty percent (50%) of the estimated cost. The description of an eligible bidder is contained in the Bidding Documents, particularly, in Section 5 of the Instructions to Bidders, and Sub-sections 5.2 and 5.4 of the Bid Data Sheet.

3) This package is one of four (4) Middle Mile Level 1 packages being procured separately by the DICT:

a) Regional Cluster 1 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Northern Mindanao and CARAGA (Region 10 and Region 13), PH-DICT-562651-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 300,747,372.00;
b) Regional Cluster 2 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Davao and SOCCSKSARGEN Mindanao (Regions 11 and 12), PH-DICT-562839-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 431,793,643.00;
c) Regional Cluster 3 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Zamboanga Peninsula and Northern Mindanao (Regions 9 and BARMM), PH-DICT-562841-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 519,159,934.00;
d) Regional Cluster 4 — Design and Build of the Phase 4 and 5 Middle Mile Level 1 Fiber Optic Cable for Western, Central, Eastern & Negros Island Visayas (Regions 6, 7, 8 and NIR) of the National Broadband Program, PH-DICT-562842-CW-RFB, EPC PHP 491,959,375.00.

A Bidder may submit a bid for one or more of these packages. Where a Bidder submits bids for more than one package, the minimum Average Annual Turnover and Liquidity required of that Bidder is the sum of the amounts required for all packages for which it submits a bid, and the Bidder shall submit the Declaration of Multi-Package Bidding required under Sub-section 5.4 (iii) of the Bid Data Sheet.

4) Bidding will be conducted in accordance with relevant procedures for open competitive bidding as specified in the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Republic Act (RA) 12009, otherwise known as the “New Government Procurement Act”, with some amendments, as stated in the Bidding Documents and is open to all Bidders from eligible source countries, as defined in the World Bank Procurement Regulations. The contract shall be awarded to the Bidder that met the criteria indicated in the Bidding Documents.

5) Interested bidders may obtain further information from the DICT and inspect the Bidding Documents at the address given below from Monday to Thursday, at 8:00 am to 6:00 pm.

6) A complete set of Bidding Documents may be acquired by interested bidders on 21 August 2026 from the address below and upon payment of the Bidding Documents fee of Ten Thousand Pesos (PhP 10,000.00)1.
It may also be downloaded from the Modernized Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System (mPhilGEPS) and the website of the Procuring Entity, provided that bidders shall pay the said Bidding Documents fee not later than the submission of their bids.

A. Department of Information and Communications Technology
BAC Secretariat, 19th Floor, DICT Headquarters Studio 7, 807 EDSA, Diliman, Quezon City, 1103 Metro Manila
Website: www.dict.gov.ph

B. e-Procurement System Website

7) The DICT will hold a Pre-Bid Conference on 02 September 2026, 10:00 A.M. Manila Time at the DICT Procurement Service, 19th Floor, DICT Headquarters, Studio 7, 807 Epifanio de los Santos Avenue, Diliman, Quezon City, 1103 Metro Manila and through video conferencing via Google Meet Platform and/or any other online video conferencing facilities, which shall be open to prospective bidders. All prospective bidders are advised to contact the BAC Secretariat through email at bac.secretariat@dict.gov.ph or landline no. (02) 8-920-01-01 loc. 6108, in advance or prior to the scheduled procurement activity, to get log-in details for the Google Meet.

8) Bids must be duly received by the Bids and Awards Committee (BAC) Secretariat through manual submission and upon presentation of the official receipt as proof of payment of the bid documents fee at the address indicated below on or before 14 September 2026, 11:00 A.M. Manila time. Late bids shall not be accepted. Bid proposals may be submitted by authorized representatives of the bidder or through courier. Interested bidders that submit bids through courier must make sure that the bid document fees are paid and the copy of the official receipt be submitted to the BAC Secretariat through bac.secretariat@dict.gov.ph or on or before the deadline of submission of bids. Bidding documents fee may be paid through the following:

a. Cash at the office address indicated below;
b. Bank Transfer (For account details, please contact the BAC Secretariat); or
c. Other modes of payment through the DICT eProcurement system which may be accessed at https://eprocurement.dict.gov.ph.

For submission of bids through courier service, bidders are reminded that the courier service personnel must submit the bid proposal to a personnel of the BAC Secretariat Division at the office address provided below. Bid submission/proposal left by the courier service personnel at the lobby guard or any other personnel or staff aside from the authorized BAC Secretariat personnel will not be considered “submitted” for purposes of bid opening. The responsibility to ensure that the courier service personnel submit the bid proposal to the authorized BAC Secretariat personnel is the sole responsibility of the prospective bidder.

Department of Information and Communications Technology
BAC Secretariat, 19th Floor, DICT Headquarters
Studio 7, 807 EDSA, Diliman, Quezon City, 1103 Metro Manila

Bidders are reminded that entry inside the DICT premises is subject to the safety and security protocols in place and processing of payment for the bidding documents prior to the submission of the actual bid offer may take time. Presence in the DICT premises and/or leaving a bid proposal/submission with the lobby guards by the bidder, bidder’s authorized representative or courier service personnel do not constitute “submission on time” which shall refer to the actual hand-over of the bid proposal to the authorized personnel of the BAC Secretariat.

8) All Bids must be accompanied by a Bid Securing Declaration.

9) Bid opening shall be on 14 September 2026, 11:00 A.M. Manila time at the DICT Procurement Service, 19th Floor, DICT Headquarters, Studio 7, 807 Epifanio de los Santos Avenue, Diliman, Quezon City, 1103 Metro Manila and through video conferencing via Google Meet Platform and/or any other online video conferencing facilities, which shall be open to prospective bidders. Bids will be opened in the presence of the Bidders’ representatives who choose to attend the activity.

10) The award criteria for this project shall be Lowest Calculated Responsive Bid (LCRB).

11) The DICT reserves the right to reject any and all bids, declare a failure of bidding, or not award the contract at any time prior to contract award in accordance with Section 70 of R.A. No. 12009, without thereby incurring any liability to the affected bidder or bidders.

12) For further information, please refer to:
